    #142227. A trading strategy to ride out the Nvidia uncertainty and generate income in the process

    📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (622 w)
    📖 Baca
    Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    A trading strategy to ride out the Nvidia uncertainty and generate income in the process

    📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (622 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Jensen Huang's abrupt resignation has sent shockwaves through the tech sector, dragging Nvidia's (NVDA) stock down roughly 30% since Oct.
    • However, for opportunistic investors, this panic has made the stock cheaper (obviously) while options have become significantly more expensive.
    • Sources indicate that buying good companies at a discount is investing 101, but the current market dynamics may do something else for those who use options.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Jensen Huang's abrupt resignation has sent shockwaves through the tech sector, dragging Nvidia's (NVDA) stock down roughly 30% since Oct. 6. The market despises uncertainty, and losing a visionary founder, particularly one without a well-telegraphed succession plan, makes it worse.

    However, for opportunistic investors, this panic has made the stock cheaper (obviously) while options have become significantly more expensive. Trading in the $160s, Nvidia's valuation has taken a big haircut, yet its underlying business fundamentals remain largely intact. While Huang was the architect of Nvidia's AI dominance, the company's moat — superior GPUs, the CUDA software ecosystem, and networking expertise — does not walk out the door with him. The company's structural advantage in the global artificial intelligence rollout persists.

    Sources indicate that buying good companies at a discount is investing 101, but the current market dynamics may do something else for those who use options. Huang's departure guarantees that Nvidia will be operating under a cloud of transition for the foreseeable future. Executing a permanent CEO search while navigating global regulatory scrutiny takes time. Consequently, Nvidia's implied volatility (IV)—the market's pricing of expected future price swings — has spiked to highs not seen since the tariff tantrum in the first half of 2025, and this elevated IV is highly likely to persist for several months as the leadership drama slowly unfolds.

    According to recent reports, this prolonged period of high implied volatility can be a goldmine for option sellers, specifically those executing options overlays such as covered call strategies. When you buy NVDA shares at these depressed levels and simultaneously sell out-of-the-money call options against your position, the premiums you collect are directly tied to IV. Because fear and transition-related uncertainty have dramatically inflated these option prices, the income generated from selling covered calls is now significantly higher than usual.

    This lowers the risk profile of holding the stock considerably over time. Consistently collecting these inflated premiums systematically lowers your overall cost basis in the underlying shares. If the stock trades sideways or recovers slowly during the CEO search, you are generating an outsized cash yield on a stagnant asset. If the stock experiences further downside turbulence, the heavy premium income acts as a substantial downside buffer, meaningfully reducing the strategy's overall risk over time.

    By deploying a persistent covered call strategy, investors can leverage the exact fear driving the stock down to generate robust, risk-reducing income while maintaining exposure to the undeniable future of AI.

    Yemen's Houthis claim attacks on Saudi oil refinery as Trump warns of fresh strikes next year

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (577 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that yemen's Houthis, backed by Iran, said Sunday that they had targeted Rabigh oil refinery in Saudi Arabia, in the latest sign of worsening hostilities in the region, as Iranian forces seek to pressure the U.S.
    • The Houthis mentioned they has directly hit the infrastructure, though the extent of the damage remains unclear, Reuters reported.
    • The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said earlier in the day that it had "intercepted and destroyed" a drone launched by the Houthis toward Saudi Arabia's western region, which included some of the country's critical energy refining and export infrastructure.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that yemen's Houthis, backed by Iran, said Sunday that they had targeted Rabigh oil refinery in Saudi Arabia, in the latest sign of worsening hostilities in the region, as Iranian forces seek to pressure the U.S. into accepting its terms.

    The Houthis mentioned they has directly hit the infrastructure, though the extent of the damage remains unclear, Reuters reported.

    The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said earlier in the day that it had "intercepted and destroyed" a drone launched by the Houthis toward Saudi Arabia's western region, which included some of the country's critical energy refining and export infrastructure.

    Rabigh, about 165 kilometers north of Jeddah on the kingdom's western Red Sea coast, hosts Petro Rabigh, a major oil refining and petrochemical complex, developed by Saudi Aramco and Japan's Sumitomo Chemical.

    Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Interior did not immediately respond to CNBC's request for comment.

    Gulf countries reported multiple attacks by Iran-linked forces over the weekend, even as the country's foreign minister mentioned his government remains open to a negotiated end to the war. Bahrain authorities said an Iranian attack on a civilian industrial facility injured two people on Saturday.

    The string of attacks mark the latest sign of escalation in the regional hostilities since the war between the U.S.-Israel and Iran began in late February, as negotiators have so far failed to agree on terms to end the monthslong war.

    The conflict has drawn in countries in the Gulf region, disrupting energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz, which used to carry a fifth of the world's crude shipments prior to the war, pushing up global prices for oil and commodities.

    The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations reported another incident involving a tanker and military forces in the Gulf of Oman on Sunday, after two tankers were struck by unknown projectiles the day before. The maritime agency gave no further details about the incident, urging vessels to stay vigilant about the operational environment.

    It has been revealed that tehran has indicated its intention to end the war with the U.S. through diplomacy, but President Donald Trump has dismissed Iranian proposals. Both sides have been in indirect communication via Qatar.

    Sources indicate that in an interview to Fox News on Saturday, Trump warned that he was inclined to order military strikes against Tehran next year, if the two countries failed to finalize an agreement. The president blamed the Iranian officials for stalling while escalating hostilities after the U.S. elections.

    "They're more aggressive now than before the election," Trump mentioned, describing Iranian officials as "professional tap dancers." "They talk all the time, all they do is talk," he added.

    The president has previously stated that Tehran wants a deal to end hostilities but not one that is "acceptable" to him. He has oscillated between favoring an agreement that would end the fighting and insisting that the U.S. does not need to rush into any deal and is not afraid of resuming more aggressive attacks.

    The Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi stated Saturday after a two-hour meeting with visiting Qatari mediators that, "We are in contact with mediators, including the Qataris, both in person and virtually, and are holding the necessary discussions to see whether another opportunity can be given to diplomacy," according to Reuters.

    International benchmark Brent futures inched 0.22% lower to $92.35 per barrel in early Asia trading hours, while WTI crude was down 0.19% at $83.25 a barrel.

    #142212. Breaking: Investors give a thumbs down to Tata Steel-APL Apollo $1.67 billion deal, plunging shares

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (433 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: Investors give a thumbs down to Tata Steel-APL Apollo $1.67 billion deal, plunging shares

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (433 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Tata Steel, one of the world's leading steel producers, on Monday noted it will buy a 26.4% stake in India's largest structural steel pipe and tube maker, APL Apollo, for 155.1 billion rupees ($1.67 billion).
    • The acquisition will boost Tata Steel's downstream integration to around 53% from 35%, the company said in a stock exchange filing.
    • Investors reacted negatively to the deal, with shares of Tata Steel sliding over 9% on Monday, while APL Apollo's stock crashed more than 19%.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Tata Steel, one of the world's leading steel producers, on Monday noted it will buy a 26.4% stake in India's largest structural steel pipe and tube maker, APL Apollo, for 155.1 billion rupees ($1.67 billion).

    The acquisition will boost Tata Steel's downstream integration to around 53% from 35%, the company said in a stock exchange filing. That will lead to more value addition, improved product mix, and greater exposure to higher-margin downstream segments, it said.

    Investors reacted negatively to the deal, with shares of Tata Steel sliding over 9% on Monday, while APL Apollo's stock crashed more than 19%.

    While the deal is likely to be positive in the long term, the complex structure and lack of clarity have rattled investors, Deven Choksey, founder and managing director of wealth management firm DRChoksey FinServ, told CNBC.

    As per Tata Steel, before acquiring APL Apollo, it will sell its steel tubes business and Tata Steel Colors to APL Apollo for 280 billion rupees. "APL Apollo will initially fund the acquisition through a mix of acquisition financing and subsequently replace the debt with long-term capitalization," Tata Steel said.

    "The deal is appearing very complex," said Choksey, adding that minority investors have not been given any clarity or taken into consideration while signing this deal.

    Tata Steel will hold an investor call, post-market hours on Monday.

    APL Apollo said after the deal it aims to more than double the downstream capacity to 15.5 million tons from the current 7.5 million tons, making it a leading global downstream steel firm.

    This capacity addition will be completed by 2035 and would include around 9 million tons per annum of steel tubes and around 6.5 million tons per annum of color-coated products, as per Tata Steel.

    Tata Steel will acquire a stake from existing shareholders of APL Apollo for 2,100 rupees per share and will ​also make an open offer to acquire an additional 26% ‌stake for 2,301.40 rupees a piece.

    In a recent development, if the open offer is successful, Tata Steel would get a controlling stake of 52.38% in APL Apollo. World's second-largest steel maker ArcelorMittal was also reportedly in the fray to acquire APL Apollo.

    The acquisition of APL Apollo would "create a downstream powerhouse for the future" that will serve the growing Indian market, T V Narendran, chief executive and managing director of Tata Steel, noted in the release.

    Tata Steel, which has an annual crude steel capacity of over 35 million tons per annum, is one of the world's most geographically diversified steel producers with presence across India, Europe and Thailand.

    #142209. Berkshire breaks out to record high with fourth-quarter rally reaching 19%

    📅 14 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1105 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Berkshire breaks out to record high with fourth-quarter rally reaching 19%

    📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1105 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Berkshire Hathaway's red-hot shares are ending a strong week with four consecutive fresh record high closes.
    • Since the rally began with the start of the fourth quarter on October 1, the Class A shares have closed at record highs 11 times as they soared 19.1%.
    • The much more widely held B shares closed at upcoming highs just 10 times but are also up 19.1% from their near-term low.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Berkshire Hathaway's red-hot shares are ending a strong week with four consecutive fresh record high closes.

    Since the rally began with the start of the fourth quarter on October 1, the Class A shares have closed at record highs 11 times as they soared 19.1%.

    The much more widely held B shares closed at upcoming highs just 10 times but are also up 19.1% from their near-term low.

    The gains are in sharp contrast to the S&P 500's 1.2% dip as investors appear to be seeing Berkshire as a relatively safe haven amid worries about AI stocks and spending.

    Both Berkshire classes were up 3.9% on the week as the S&P advanced by 2.5%, its best week since early August.

    Berkshire's B shares are now 7.5 percentage points ahead of the benchmark for the year so far.

    After erasing their post-Buffett CEO announcement losses three weeks ago, Berkshire shares are now up almost 10% since last year's shareholders meeting.

    They've gained around 29% since last August's lows and are up around 18% year-to-date.

    Berkshire Hathaway is due to disclose its quarterly equity portfolio snapshot on Monday when it files its Q3 13F with the SEC.

    We won't know for sure until then, but numbers in the company's third quarter 10-Q, released last Saturday, indicate Berkshire continued to reduce its Bank of America stake.

    It would be the ninth consecutive quarter of selling.

    As of June 30, Berkshire reported holding 483.4 million BAC shares valued now at $24.7 billion, it's fifth largest equity position.

    On June 30, 2024, before the selling began, Berkshire owned just over 1 billion shares valued at $41.1 billion.

    Since then, the number of shares in the portfolio has decreased by 53.2%, not including any Q3 sales, while the stock price has increased by 28.3%.

    If there had been no reductions, the position would be worth $52.7 billion.

    The belief Berkshire sold more BAC shares in the third quarter is based on a $372 million reduction in the cost basis for equities categorized by the manufacturer as "banks, insurance, and finance.".

    The 10-Q also reports $2.2 billion of pretax gains from equity sales.

    Recent findings suggest that barron's notes Bank of America and American Express are the only financial stocks in the portfolio that have a cost basis low enough to generate a gain like that. Amex is one of the four stocks new CEO Greg Abel indicated would be held for "decades" to come in his February letter to shareholders.

    In any case, Berkshire's almost 23% stake in Amex would have required it to swiftly disclose any sales.

    Based on the numbers in the 10-Q, the warrants Berkshire received as part of a 2011 $5 billion investment in the bank that it used in 2017 to buy 700 million shares at $7.14 each, and BAC's average stock price in the quarter, Barron's estimates 30 to 40 million shares may have been sold.

    That would be roughly in line with the 30.2 million shares sold in the second quarter.

    The case isn't as good, but Barron's thinks Berkshire may have bought more Alphabet shares in the period. That's based on a $2.3 billion increase in the cost basis for the category that includes Google's parent.

    Overall, it looks like it will be a relatively quiet quarter with $2.4 billion in equity purchases and $2.8 billion in sales.

    In the first quarter, Berkshire bought $15.9 billion and sold $24.1 billion of equities. In the second quarter, it purchased $23.5 billion and sold $3.7 billion.

    All those numbers exclude the company's buybacks of its own stock.

    In a term sheet filed early Friday, Berkshire Hathaway notes it is selling more than 182 billion yen ($1.1 billion) worth of bonds with maturities between 2029 and 2056 and annual interest rates between 2.6% and 4.6%.

    Bloomberg points out the rates, compared to benchmarks, are higher than its previous sale this year.

    It quotes a fund manager as saying market sentiment "has become more sensitive," forcing issuers to make their offerings more attractive.

    In April, Berkshire sold 272 billion yen ($1.7 billion) of bonds.

    Berkshire uses the proceeds from the yen-denominated bonds to protect its ongoing investments in Japanese stocks from currency fluctuations.

    Some links may require a subscription:.

    Warren Buffett recommends Benjamin Graham's book, "The Intelligent Investor," and outlines what he considers Graham's three most important ideas.

    WARREN BUFFETT: On investment books, if you're asking about that, I would recommend the first two books that Phil Fisher wrote back around 1960, "Common Sense [Stocks] and Uncommon Profits" and the second one ["Paths to Wealth Through Common Stocks"]. They're very good books.

    You know, I obviously recommend, first and foremost, [Benjamin Graham's] "The Intelligent Investor," with chapters eight and 20 are the ones that you really should read.

    Recent findings suggest that two of the — well, all of the important ideas in investing, really, are in that book, because there's only about three ideas. And those — two of them are emphasized in those two chapters...

    One is that — to think of yourself — to think of investing as owning a business and not buying something that wiggles around in price.

    According to recent reports, and the second one is your attitude, which ties in with that, the attitude toward the market, that's covered in chapter eight. And if you have the proper attitude toward market movements, it's an enormous help in securities.

    And the final chapter is on the margin of safety, which means, don't try and drive a 9,800-pound truck over a bridge that indicates it's, you know, "Capacity: 10,000 pounds." But go down the road a little bit and find one that says, "Capacity: 15,000 pounds.".

    Berkshire market capitalization: $1,259,897,054,755.

    Berkshire Cash as of Sept 30: $377.4 billion (Up 3.3% from June 30).

    Excluding Rail Cash and Subtracting T-Bills Payable: $352.3 billion (Down 1.9% from June 30).

    Berkshire repurchased $9.6 billion of its shares in Q3 2026.

    #142195. Social Security benefits are rising in 2027, but other changes could affect what you keep

    📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1145 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Social Security benefits are rising in 2027, but other changes could affect what you keep

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1145 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Whether you're working or retired, changes to Social Security in 2027 could affect your finances.
    • Sources indicate that starting in January, millions of program beneficiaries will get a 3.6% increase to their benefits, thanks to the annual cost-of-living adjustment.
    • Meanwhile, a higher taxable earnings cap means some workers will pay Social Security taxes on more income, reducing their paycheck.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Whether you're working or retired, changes to Social Security in 2027 could affect your finances.

    Sources indicate that starting in January, millions of program beneficiaries will get a 3.6% increase to their benefits, thanks to the annual cost-of-living adjustment. But rising Medicare premiums could chip away at the increase — and as beneficiaries' incomes rise, that may affect the taxes they owe and their eligibility for a latest senior deduction.

    Meanwhile, a higher taxable earnings cap means some workers will pay Social Security taxes on more income, reducing their paycheck.

    Here's a breakdown of what to expect in the new year.

    Social Security's limit for payroll taxes is adjusted every year to reflect the average wage index.

    In a recent development, in 2027, the taxable maximum will go up to $192,300 in earnings, up from $184,500 in 2026. Workers and employers each pay a 6.2% payroll tax on earnings up to that limit — or 12.4% for self-employed workers. Medicare taxes of 1.45% for both workers and employers are not subject to a limit.

    In 2027, workers who earn $192,300 or more will pay $11,922.60 in total Social Security payroll taxes, according to the Social Security Administration, while self-employed workers will pay $23,845.20.

    "If you're somebody whose income is over what the new threshold is going to be, this increase in the threshold results in a tax increase to you," said Tim Steffen, director of advanced planning at financial services firm Baird.

    The 3.6% Social Security cost-of-living adjustment for 2027 is slated to increase retirement benefits by about $75 per month on average, according to the Social Security Administration.

    According to recent reports, the annual adjustment is the largest boost to benefits since 2023 due to rising inflation. The COLA averaged 2.6% from 2000 to 2026, according to the Senior Citizens League, a nonpartisan senior group.

    Around 72 million Social Security beneficiaries will see benefit increases, according to the agency.

    In a recent development, the maximum benefit for a worker at full retirement age — when individuals become eligible for 100% of the benefits they've earned — will rise to $4,188 per month in 2027, up from $4,152 per month in 2026, according to the federal agency. To be eligible for the maximum benefit at full retirement age — typically age 66 to 67 — you generally have to earn up to the taxable threshold for each of your working years factored into the calculation.

    How much of the COLA increase Social Security beneficiaries see depends in part on their Medicare premiums, which may be deducted directly from benefit checks.

    Monthly rates are poised to increase for both Medicare Part B, which covers medically necessary services and preventive care, and Part D, which provides prescription drug coverage.

    The standard monthly Medicare Part B premium will be $209.40 in 2027 — a $6.50 increase from $202.90 in 2026, according to the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services.

    "It's not often that we see a Part B [premium] increase that is lower than the COLA," Mary Johnson, an independent Social Security and Medicare policy analyst, said of the 3.2% increase. The last time that happened was in 2023, she said.

    Medicare Part D beneficiaries may also pay higher premiums in 2027.

    Recent findings suggest that assuming enrollees keep the same plan, the average enrollment-weighted monthly Part D premium may be $51 in 2027, up 50% from $34 in 2026, according to projections from KFF, a provider of health policy research and polling. That is higher than CMS' projections, which forecast the national average premium for standalone Part D looks will rise about $1, to $36, in 2027 from $35 in 2026.

    It has been revealed that standard monthly premiums for Part B and plan-specific premiums for Part D apply to individuals who have $112,000 or less in modified adjusted gross income, or $224,000 for married couples. Beneficiaries with higher income pay larger premiums because of income-related monthly adjustment amounts, which affect 9% of Medicare Part B and Part D beneficiaries, according to CMS.

    With bigger Social Security benefits, more households may find that some portion of benefits is taxable — though a newly introduced senior deduction may help provide some relief to those who are eligible.

    Social Security benefits may be subject to federal income taxes for certain individuals. The thresholds at which those taxes are applied are not adjusted from year to year.

    Whether or not benefits are taxed is determined by a formula known as combined income — the sum of adjusted gross income, tax-exempt interest income and half of Social Security benefits:.

    Individuals who are subject to taxes may opt to withhold taxes from their Social Security benefit checks, rather than face a potential bill during tax filing season.

    Separately, a temporary senior deduction of up to $6,000 for individuals ages 65 and over may help to indirectly reduce taxes on Social Security benefits.

    That deduction, part of the One Significant Beautiful Bill Act in 2025, helps reduce retirees' taxable income, according to Steffen. It's in place through 2028. Because the break phases out for individuals with modified adjusted gross income starting at $75,000 — and for married couples with $150,000 — it's vital to watch your income if you're close to those limits, Steffen noted.

    Sources indicate that "Keep in mind that if you're over 65, you might qualify for this deduction," Steffen noted. "But if you let your income get too big, you might lose the deduction.".

    Moreover, any extra income that causes you to lose the deduction may also come with its own taxes, making it more expensive, according to Steffen.

    Industry observers note that "What we've been telling our clients is that tax planning is a lot more complicated than it used to be, and you can't do it on the back of an envelope anymore," he said. "You need to use good tools that can do good calculations for you.".

    Individuals who claim Social Security retirement benefits before their full retirement age and who continue to work may be subject to withholdings.

    Industry observers note that in 2027, individuals under full retirement age may earn up to $25,560 per year, up from $24,480 in 2026, without adjustments to their Social Security benefits. For every $2 in earnings above that limit, $1 in Social Security benefits will be withheld.

    According to recent reports, importantly, those withholdings are not lost completely. Once a beneficiary reaches full retirement age, the withheld money will be credited to their benefits over their remaining lifespan.

    In the year individuals reach full retirement age, the retirement earnings test limit is higher — $67,920 per year in 2027, up from $65,160 per year in 2026. For every $3 in earnings above that limit, $1 in Social Security benefits is withheld.

    Starting the month a beneficiary reaches full retirement age, no earnings are withheld.

    JPMorgan's top books and experiences for the wealthy this holiday season

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (837 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Morgan released its list of recommended books and experiences for clients, including legendary investor David Booth's latest book, a longevity clinic in Thailand and a dance-floor adaptation of "Much Ado About Nothing" on Broadway.
    • The "NextList 2026" begins with submissions from J.P.
    • In a recent development, "Geopolitics was a top concern.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    J.P. Morgan released its list of recommended books and experiences for clients, including legendary investor David Booth's latest book, a longevity clinic in Thailand and a dance-floor adaptation of "Much Ado About Nothing" on Broadway.

    The "NextList 2026" begins with submissions from J.P. Morgan client advisors, which are narrowed down by a review committee. The list also reflects findings from the bank's global family office survey, which tracks the concerns and interests of ultra-high-net-worth clients, stated Darin Oduyoye, JPMorgan Asset & Wealth Management's chief communications officer.

    In a recent development, "Geopolitics was a top concern. And as AI continues to be a prominent conversation, clients are looking for perspective on the forces shaping markets," Oduyoye told CNBC. "Specifically, David Booth's story, from selling shoes as a teenager in Kansas to launching the first index fund, offers time-tested wisdom on investing. It's a reminder to look beyond short-term market swings and stay focused on your long-term goals.".

    Industry observers note that with familiar names like Paddington Bear and a commemorative book to celebrate the 125th anniversary of Bergdorf Goodman among this year's picks, the list has a strong note of nostalgia. On the inclusion of books by David Rubenstein, Angela Duckworth and Danny Meyer, Oduyoye said, "Their ideas on leadership continue to resonate in a rapidly changing world, reflecting a desire for trusted voices and enduring wisdom amid the noise.".

    At the same time, clients are looking to discover new experiences, especially overseas, he mentioned.

    According to recent reports, here is the full J.P. Morgan NextList 2026, including the bank's descriptions of recommended items. The entries have been lightly edited for style.

    Clinique La Prairie, Phuket, Thailand.

    The Swiss longevity clinic Clinique La Prairie has brought its signature approach to Phuket with a retreat at Tri Vananda. The program pairs medical science with personalized nutrition, movement and well-being, and guests leave with a plan to support long-term health.

    Fondazione Dries Van Noten, Venice, Italy.

    Created by designer Dries Van Noten and his partner, Patrick Vangheluwe, the foundation explores craftsmanship from fashion to ceramics through exhibitions, residencies and talks. Its opening presentation, The Only True Protest Is Beauty, explores beauty and creative heritage.

    International Dark Sky Discovery Center, Fountain Hills, Arizona.

    Opening in early 2027, the center will offer an immersive experience of the night sky with a planetarium, observatory and interactive exhibits. Lectures and public viewing nights will invite visitors to experience the truly dark skies.

    La Hacienda Clase Azul, Jalisco, Mexico.

    According to recent reports, developed by tequila brand Clase Azul México, the 50-acre estate combines tequila production with artisan workshops dedicated to the brand's signature handmade decanters. Visitors can explore spaces celebrating regional heritage and dine at OYA, which focuses on traditional Mexican cuisine.

    Suzhou Museum of Contemporary Art, Suzhou, China.

    It has been revealed that the new 59,500-square-meter museum sits beside Jinji Lake's "Suzhou's Eye" Ferris wheel. The large-scale public museum allows visitors to wander through a garden of pavilions and courtyards connected by art-filled galleries and porticoes.

    Opening in June 2027 on Norway's northern coast, the museum will explore whale biology, evolution and ecology through exhibitions that blend science and art. The multisensory experience aims to deepen visitors' understanding of the scale, intelligence and mystery of the world's largest mammals.

    "DOLLY: A True Original Musical," St. James Theatre.

    In a recent development, the fresh musical follows Dolly Parton's journey from the Smoky Mountains to global superstardom, featuring hits including "Jolene" and "9 to 5," as well as new songs by Parton. Directed by Bartlett Sher, it celebrates the ambition and reinvention behind her career. Previews begin December 7.

    "Much Ado About Nothing," Winter Garden Theatre.

    Tom Hiddleston ("Loki," "The Night Manager") and Hayley Atwell ("Agent Carter") star as Benedick and Beatrice in Shakespeare's battle of wits. Directed by Tony Award winner Jamie Lloyd, the limited engagement closes Jan. 10, 2027.

    "Paddington The Musical," Al Hirschfeld Theatre.

    The seven-time Olivier Award-winning London hit brings the beloved bear to Broadway. The imaginative musical, which celebrates kindness, belonging and adventure, begins previews on March 30, 2027.

    "Purple Rain," Majestic Theatre.

    According to recent reports, inspired by Prince's Grammy-winning album and Oscar-winning film, the newly introduced musical is set in 1984 Minneapolis and features more than 20 of his songs. Tony nominee Saheem Ali directs Jordan Fisher as the magnetic new rock musician in the production, which begins previews on April 12, 2027.

    Aperture Cellars, Sonoma County, California.

    Industry observers note that the cellar was founded by acclaimed winemaker Jesse Katz, who has created more than 60 perfect 100-point wines. Aperture brings together wine, art and nature, drawing on inspiration from his father, photographer Andy Katz.

    TOR Wines, Napa Valley, California.

    Founded by Tor Kenward, the family-owned winery recently celebrated its 25th anniversary. TOR has earned more than 30 perfect 100-point scores and focuses on single-vineyard Cabernet Sauvignon and Chardonnay made in limited quantities.

    #142187. Industry News: Stop agonizing over the ‘right’ choice—to avoid regret, save time and reduce stress, take these 3 steps

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1064 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: Stop agonizing over the ‘right’ choice—to avoid regret, save time and reduce stress, take these 3 steps

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1064 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • If you want to be successful in your career, your ability to make a decision, map out a plan and take swift action is crucial.
    • Sources indicate that in 70% of the 20 fastest-growing occupations, as identified by the Bureau of Labor Statistics, judgment and decision-making are considered key soft skills, according to a ResumeNow report published Nov.
    • When the time comes to make an important decision, you naturally want to get it right.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    If you want to be successful in your career, your ability to make a decision, map out a plan and take swift action is crucial.

    Sources indicate that in 70% of the 20 fastest-growing occupations, as identified by the Bureau of Labor Statistics, judgment and decision-making are considered key soft skills, according to a ResumeNow report published Nov. 12. A November 2025 report from the Burning Glass Institute found that decision-making skills — including problem-solving, risk analysis and strategic thinking — were "one of the most enduring and economically valuable human capabilities" in the age of artificial intelligence, with 41% of more than 6.8 million U.S. job postings from 2022 to 2024 explicitly mentioning them.

    When the time comes to make an important decision, you naturally want to get it right. So you might research, examine every variable and analyze the data, only to find yourself completely unable to move forward. This analysis paralysis is often rooted in perfectionism, as you tell yourself: "I need to make the absolute best choice…".

    The problem with this mindset is that there's no such thing as a perfect choice. As a cognitive behavioral psychotherapist who specializes in anxiety and works with high performers, I know that maximizing — the never-ending quest to find a flawless or ideal choice — is a trap.

    Sources indicate that in my experience, the happiest and most successful professionals don't waste time hunting for a flawless path or agonize over making the "right" decision. They pick a direction and channel their energy into making that decision work.

    Landmark research by psychologist Barry Schwartz, author of "The Paradox of Choice," and his colleagues highlights that "maximizers" who obsess over finding the single best option end up experiencing higher levels of regret and depression and lower well-being than "satisficers," who settle on a solid choice that meets their core standards. Maximizing squanders precious time, energy and resources, and leads to choice overload, elevated anxiety and lower overall satisfaction.

    Coming from a cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) perspective — where the core idea is that our thoughts affect how we feel, our feelings affect how we behave and our behaviors reinforce our thoughts — maximizing is rooted in unhelpful thinking styles called cognitive distortions. These patterned, habitual ways of thinking aren't necessarily based on fact, but feel compellingly true.

    Specifically, maximizers get caught in black-and-white thinking, where a choice is framed as strictly good or bad, right or wrong, smart or dumb, and in catastrophizing, which means focusing exclusively on the absolute worst-case scenario.

    These rigid, all-or-nothing thought patterns and worst-case predictions directly fuel chronic anxiety, emotional paralysis and avoidant behavior, according to foundational CBT research by Aaron Beck and Judith Beck. For example, a maximizer might spiral down this road: "If I don't make the perfect choice, I'll get fired and lose my reputation, and Brad will get my office!".

    The reality? Initial decisions rarely need to be as set in stone as we might imagine. Success is rarely about choosing the single "correct" door on the first try. It's determined by making a sound decision and executing it with a flexible, dedicated approach.

    To avoid the maximizing trap, take these steps:.

    In a recent development, maximizing is appealing because it gives you the illusion of productivity; you feel like you're working hard by pouring energy into finding the single right choice. In reality, exhaustive research can be a waste of time and mental energy.

    Sources indicate that this is why establishing "good enough" criteria is essential, based on Nobel Prize-winning economist Herbert Simon's concept of satisficing. It may feel risky at first, especially if your decision-making is being hijacked by catastrophic thoughts about worst-case scenarios. But over-analyzing is actually the riskier path.

    Start by identifying the non-negotiable criteria for success. Then make a rule that you'll spend no more than two hours on background research, consult only three resources or review just two or three vendor proposals.

    Once an option meets, say, 80% to 90% of your benchmarks, shut down the search phase and lock in your decision. Save the rest of your energy for planning and execution.

    Industry observers note that indecision and its close cousin, procrastination, function as avoidance strategies I see people use to temporarily escape short-term stress and anxiety. Time fuels analysis paralysis, and your options will feel endless if you don't set boundaries.

    Psychological research on procrastination confirms that delaying decisions can be an emotional regulation strategy rather than a time-management concern.

    To manage this anxiety loop, set a strict deadline on your calendar and commit to making a call once time is up. You can also create smaller time goals for different phases of the process, such as data gathering and resource identification.

    Remind yourself: A solid, well-executed decision made today beats a perfect decision delayed until next month.

    In a recent development, every decision you make will eventually be subject to change. The more valuable skill isn't finding the ultimate answer, but cultivating flexibility and adaptability.

    Clinical research on psychological flexibility demonstrates that the ability to adapt your thinking and pivot in real time is associated with lower anxiety and greater resilience under pressure. When you learn to shift your focus from pre-decision evaluation to post-decision adaptability, you can make almost any sound choice the right choice.

    When you have thoughts like "I have to make the right choice," try to reframe them by asking yourself instead: "How will I pivot if this doesn't go according to plan?".

    It makes sense to want to get things right from the start. But even the most successful people aren't fortune tellers. So instead of front-loading the task by pouring valuable time and energy into maximizing, top performers save their precious resources for execution — and have the confidence to know they can handle the outcomes as they unfold.

    Recent findings suggest that chamin Ajjan, LCSW, A-CBT, CST is the CEO and Clinical Director of Chamin Ajjan Psychotherapy, a regional clinic of the National Social Anxiety Center where she is also a board member. She completed her undergraduate work at the University of California, Berkeley, and graduate school at Columbia University School of Social Work. She is also the author of "Seeking Soulmate: Ditch The Dating Game and Find Real Connection.″.

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (960 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    ‘Worst COP ever’: Climate talks collapse after draft deal fails to include fossil fuels

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (960 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Negotiations at the United Nations' climate summit collapsed on Sunday as the U.K., EU and others rejected a draft deal that failed to include fossil fuels.
    • Since the U.N.'s Climate Change Conference — or COP31 — began in Antalya, Turkey, on Nov.
    • Antonio Guterres, the U.N.'s secretary-general, mentioned he was "deeply disappointed" that no consensus was reached.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Negotiations at the United Nations' climate summit collapsed on Sunday as the U.K., EU and others rejected a draft deal that failed to include fossil fuels.

    Since the U.N.'s Climate Change Conference — or COP31 — began in Antalya, Turkey, on Nov. 9, almost 200 countries have been locked in talks to reach a "cover decision," with a number of drafts issued in recent days.

    Antonio Guterres, the U.N.'s secretary-general, mentioned he was "deeply disappointed" that no consensus was reached.

    Talks centered on electrification, funding for developing nations and ways to respond to scientific warnings about rising global temperatures, with the 1.5 degrees Celsius target likely to be overshot.

    But on Sunday, after negotiations overran by almost two days, the latest cover proposal made no mention of fossil fuels, prompting outcry from governments and campaigners.

    Recent findings suggest that speaking on behalf of the EU, Ireland's climate minister Darragh O'Brien said the conference was "hijacked by some oil states," when asked by Reuters about Saudi Arabia's role in the negotiations. CNBC has contacted Saudi Arabia for comment.

    The EU mentioned it rejected the deal because the text "does not respond to the science" of climate change. "We will not accept a COP that greenwashes fossil fuels," it said in a statement Sunday.

    In a recent development, the U.K. government "does not believe the cover decision proposed by the Presidencies meets the moment," it said on Sunday. "It moves us backwards on the science when we must accelerate implementation," it said.

    Recent findings suggest that representatives of island nations — vulnerable to the effects of climate change — refused to sign the draft text. "Three years ago in Dubai, the nations of the world agreed by consensus to transition away from fossil fuels in their energy systems," Philip Davis, prime minister of the Bahamas, said in an online statement, referring to the UAE Consensus made at COP28 in 2023.

    In a recent development, "Small island states produce less than 1% of global emissions, yet we carry the weight of a crisis we did not cause. We have brought looks, commitments and patience to three decades of these talks. Antalya exhausted that patience," Davis said.

    Albert Salamanca, a senior research fellow at the Stockholm Environment Institute Asia, told CNBC via email that the lack of consensus on a deal is "tantamount to a death sentence for vulnerable communities still unable to respond in a timely manner to emerging risks.".

    Developing nations are facing "abandonment," according to Mohamed Adow, director of climate and energy think tank Power Shift Africa. He described the event as "the worst COP ever" in an online statement, adding that "rich countries blocked the creation of a just transition mechanism.".

    The World Wildlife Fund, or WWF, described the lack of progress on finance for developing nations as having "real-world consequences for the lives and livelihoods of the planet's most vulnerable communities," in an online statement.

    Nonsikelelo Nkomo-Mabobe, business development manager at Solidaridad, an organization that promotes fair supply chains, welcomed some of the language in COP31's proposed Antalya Pact, with "promising signs around food security, which is acknowledged as heavily affected by climate impacts." But she mentioned a finance gap remains.

    "Funding must be easier for frontline communities to access, and it must be traceable once it has been disbursed," Nkomo-Mabobe remarked in an email to CNBC.

    In a recent development, the WWF welcomed the engagement from participants of the COP31 Action Agenda, which comprises of businesses and other non-governmental organizations. "Momentum from communities, cities and businesses is real despite what happened in the negotiating rooms," it said.

    A major goal of COP31 was to increase global electrification to 35% by 2035 — up from 23% today, with a Global Climate Action Agenda Electrification Delivery Package announced on Thursday as a "first milestone" to achieve this.

    In a recent development, the U.N.'s Climate Change Executive Secretary Simon Stiell stated on Sunday that "around half" the global economy is accelerating electrification, adding that the package had made "real economy" progress. More than 90 countries signed the pledge, according to Australia's Climate Change and Energy Minister Chris Bowen, COP31's president of negotiations.

    "Frustratingly," the pledge does not detail how the electricity will be generated, according to Ellen Dorsey, executive director of the Wallace Global Fund — around 57% of electricity was generated by fossil fuels in 2025, according to think tank Ember.

    Sources indicate that dorsey urged states to provide electricity to those in developing countries. "Will we ensure governments provide electricity to hundreds of millions who lack it, by leapfrogging fossil fuels build-out and instead invest in small-scale renewables?" she noted in an email to CNBC.

    Industry observers note that preserving sea life has "often been overlooked" in climate negotiations, according to the U.N. The language referring to oceans in the draft cover decision was "slightly weakened," according to Nicolas Entrup, director of international relations at marine conservation organization OceanCare, in an email to CNBC. But he said he was hopeful that the Antalya Ocean Current, a U.N. plan to hold future talks on oceans and climate change, would be carried forward.

    More than 95% of island and coastal nations now have ocean preservation in their climate plans, but around 60% of those commitments rely on external funding, according to research by ocean conservancy groups. Scientists also called for ongoing investment to monitor oceans beyond short-term research.

    It has been revealed that "I share the deep disappointment of many: COP31 has been unable to agree on problems related to both Presidency's led decisions," Stiell said. Turkey and Australia shared the presidency at this year's conference.

    - CNBC's Sawdah Bhaimiya contributed to this report.

    Clarification: This story has been updated to more accurately reflect Nicolas Entrup's comments.

    Nvidia has lost $2 trillion in value. Here's what options traders expect from earnings

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (518 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that jensen Huang's forced exit from Nvidia shocked Wall Street and Washington, wiped $2 trillion off its market value, and raised serious questions about national security and regulation of the AI complex.
    • With volatility in the stock near the highest since April 2025, options traders are now pricing a 7% reaction in the stock after its report, the biggest implied move going into an Nvidia report since February 2025, and well above the median move of 3.2% over the last eight quarters.
    • It has been revealed that implied volatility reached 68 Monday, compared to under 40 in early October, according to ThinkOrSwim data.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that jensen Huang's forced exit from Nvidia shocked Wall Street and Washington, wiped $2 trillion off its market value, and raised serious questions about national security and regulation of the AI complex. Traders, for the moment, must content themselves with the comparatively mundane business of Tuesday's earnings, and options traders are expecting big moves.

    With volatility in the stock near the highest since April 2025, options traders are now pricing a 7% reaction in the stock after its report, the biggest implied move going into an Nvidia report since February 2025, and well above the median move of 3.2% over the last eight quarters.

    It has been revealed that implied volatility reached 68 Monday, compared to under 40 in early October, according to ThinkOrSwim data. Nvidia vol reached a multi-year high above 92 in the aftermath of President Trump's tariff Liberation day in April '25. In other words, the organization that for much of the AI boom was the most reliable winner in the market, is now more volatile than all but 35 companies in the S&P 500.

    "Longer term, I see significant downside risk unless Nvidia can attract an exceptional leader, someone like Tim Cook or AMD's Lisa Su," Nigam Arora, founder of the Arora report, said in a text ahead of the firm's after-market report on Tuesday.

    Since hitting all-time highs in October, Nvidia shares have fallen 35%, shedding $2 trillion in market capitalization along the way. Including Nvidia, there are only five companies in the S&P 500 worth more than $2 trillion. However, there is evidence that bulls have been holding out hope while bears snatch up profits: the ratio of open puts to call contracts has actually widened towards calls, according to Barchart data. The ratio is right now 0.87, down from a one-year high of 1.02 two weeks ago and the lowest since the first week of October.

    The most popular contract by volume on Monday was the 155-strike put expiring at the bell Monday, but the most popular trade for later expiry was the 160-strike call expiring Thursday, and the second-most-common purchase was the 190-strike call expiring Friday, SpotGamma data show.

    Industry observers note that one catch is that most call contracts traded Monday looked like neutral to bearish positions opened by traders selling calls. Of the 5 million options traded on Monday, 3 million were calls, but more were likely opened by sellers than buyers. Of the $2.3 billion in options premium traded on Nvidia Monday, $1.2 billion was tied to puts, SpotGamma data show.

    With bears taking profits in puts the past month, there's another potential snag on open interest. There are very few open put contracts at or below the $157 level at which the stock closed Monday. That suggests any bad surprise would find many traders with little downside protection.

    By the same token, there's notable open interest in call contracts from the 175-strike and above, suggesting profit-taking on a bounce could limit Nvidia's recovery past levels it breached over the past week.

    Either way, Tuesday's earnings could provide fireworks.

    Last week's sell-off could be a dip-buyer's dream, if history repeats itself.As the Nasdaq-100 Index touched bear market territory at Friday's low, and the S&P 500 slipped to 12% off its highs, the Cboe Volatility Index (VIX) reached above 40, the highest since April 2025 and in the top 5% of readings for the so-called "fear gauge" going back to 1990, according to Charlie Bilello, chief market strategist at Creative Planning.Good news for bulls: S&P 500 returns look well above-average following such days. The one-year return after fifth-percentile VIX readings is 29%, more than double the 12% from all other VIX levels, Bilello writes. Two years later, the return is 46%, compared to 25% normally.A similar analysis by Noel Smith of Kai Asset Management shows that of the 13 times VIX has touched 40 since 1990, the median 1-month return of the S&P 500 is 3.6%, and the 3-month return 8.1%, compared to 1.2% and 3.2%, respectively, during all other times.

    According to recent reports, the sell-off was also unique in its timing on the calendar, with November traditionally the best month for stocks, data from the Stock Trader's Almanac show.The S&P's 5.6% drop from Wednesday's close through Friday was the worst Thursday/Friday combo in a week before the Thanksgiving holiday since the index started trading in 1957, according to OddStats on X.It was also only the fourth time in the history of the Invesco QQQ Trust that the fund was down at least 2% on a Thursday and 5% on Friday. The other instances were during Liberation Week last year, and two in the early dot-com bust. One of those periods is more encouraging than the other, but both led to a median 7.5% rally the next week, according to OddStats.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Shares of chipmaker Advanced Micro Devices close down 7.72% to $489.19 on Thursday after investment firm Hunterbrook Media issued a report alleging that the company "has its own China problem.".

    Hunterbrook disclosed that it had taken a short position in AMD.

    The report claims that "after the U.S. blacklisted Chinese server maker IEIT Systems, the tech giant kept getting newer AMD firmware, which enables AMD chips to run in servers.".

    CNBC did not independently verify this information.

    Hunterbrook also mentioned that newly introduced export rules in Washington could "tighten restrictions on AMD's foreign business," alleging that AMD "bills over 20% of its revenue to customers in China and Hong Kong," and "depends on a Chinese partner to finish most of its chips.".

    Recent findings suggest that the allegations come amid investigations of rival chipmaker Nvidia over its sales to companies in Asia with ties to China. AMD has been viewed as a beneficiary of the uncertainty surrounding Nvidia.

    Industry observers note that "The claims misrepresent AMD's business practices and relationships," an AMD spokesperson mentioned in a statement. "AMD complies with applicable US export control laws and regulations and maintains rigorous processes to ensure compliance across our global operations. We remain focused on serving our customers and upholding the highest standards of integrity.".

    Lisa Su, CEO of AMD, told investors on the company's recent earnings call that China is an "vital" market and that the semiconductor giant wants to be fully compliant with U.S. export controls.

    AMD continued to slide after hours, trading down 0.45% to $487 shortly after 4 p.m.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Monday lauded an "exemplary" military operation that sank one of Russia's newest ships at a Libyan port, after Kyiv's forces struck their target with several domestically made naval drones.
    • The incident followed a suspected Ukrainian drone strike on a Russian cargo ship in the Baltic Sea on Saturday and occurred less than a week after damage was inflicted on Russian President Vladimir Putin's prized Crimea bridge.
    • In a social media post, Zelenskyy remarked Ukrainian forces deployed seven sea drones to attack the Merkury, a Russian navy corvette, at Benghazi's port in the early hours of Sunday morning.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Monday lauded an "exemplary" military operation that sank one of Russia's newest ships at a Libyan port, after Kyiv's forces struck their target with several domestically made naval drones.

    The incident followed a suspected Ukrainian drone strike on a Russian cargo ship in the Baltic Sea on Saturday and occurred less than a week after damage was inflicted on Russian President Vladimir Putin's prized Crimea bridge.

    In a social media post, Zelenskyy remarked Ukrainian forces deployed seven sea drones to attack the Merkury, a Russian navy corvette, at Benghazi's port in the early hours of Sunday morning. Ukraine's president posted dramatic video footage showing Ukraine's naval drones triggering a massive explosion on the Russian ship.

    It has been revealed that "Despite all the enemy's efforts to counter the attack, the Russian corvette Merkury was sunk. It's one of their newest ships, commissioned in 2023, during the full-scale war," Zelenskyy said. "We continue our operations in designated waters," he added.

    Satellite imagery taken on Sunday indicated the Merkury mostly underwater, having capsized.

    According to recent reports, the Russian dry cargo ship MV Angara, which Zelenskyy said Moscow used to transport weapons, was hit by Ukrainian forces. A Ka-27 military helicopter on the Merkury was also destroyed.

    Asked about reports of attacks on Russian ships off the coast of Libya, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov noted information on this would be provided via the Defense Ministry.

    The Security Service of Ukraine, the SBU, mentioned Monday that the attacks "once again demonstrated that the Russian military fleet and its logistics have no safe routes even far beyond the Black Sea," according to a Google translation.

    "Such unique special operations destroy the enemy's logistical capabilities and force Russia to pay for aggression even at a strategic distance from Ukraine," the SBU said via Telegram.

    The United Nations Support Mission in Libya, or UNSMIL, expressed "serious concern" over the drone attacks in a statement saying the country "cannot afford, and must not become a battleground for foreign conflicts.".

    "UNSMIL calls for an immediate, independent and transparent investigation to establish the facts and hold those responsible to account," it added.

    The incident is not the first time Libya has seen attacks linked to the Russia-Ukraine war near its territory.

    In March, Moscow's Transport Ministry accused Ukraine of striking the Arctic Metagaz, a liquefied natural gas tanker, as part of a suspected sea drone attack in the Mediterranean between Libya and Malta.

    Industry News: Netflix’s ‘The Altruists’ sparks FTX portrayal debate among crypto bigwigs from CZ to Star Xu

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (876 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Netflix's "The Altruists," released Nov.
    • According to recent reports, critics have questioned the accuracy of the series' portrayal of the FTX collapse, particularly how it assigns responsibility of the scandal.
    • According to recent reports, zhao criticized the series in a post on X, calling it "insane" and questioning whether the show was intended to influence public perception.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Netflix's "The Altruists," released Nov. 19, has sparked backlash from prominent cryptocurrency industry figures, including Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao, over its portrayal of the collapse of FTX.

    According to recent reports, critics have questioned the accuracy of the series' portrayal of the FTX collapse, particularly how it assigns responsibility of the scandal. Several crypto industry figures argue that it softens the culpability of Sam Bankman-Fried and Caroline Ellison while casting Zhao — widely known as CZ — as an outsized villain.

    According to recent reports, zhao criticized the series in a post on X, calling it "insane" and questioning whether the show was intended to influence public perception. He declined to comment to CNBC beyond his social-media posts.

    Sources indicate that zhao pleaded guilty in 2023 to failing to maintain an effective anti-money laundering program at Binance, in violation of the U.S. Bank Secrecy Act, in a case separate from the FTX fraud. He was sentenced to four months in prison in 2024 and pardoned by President Donald Trump in October 2025.

    FTX filed for bankruptcy in November 2022 after a liquidity crisis exposed deep financial problems at the exchange. Investigations later found that billions of dollars in customer funds had been diverted to Alameda Research.

    Shortly before FTX's collapse, Zhao declared that Binance would liquidate its remaining holdings of FTT, FTX's native token, intensifying pressure on the exchange.

    Bankman-Fried was sentenced to 25 years in prison in March 2024 after being convicted of fraud and conspiracy charges. Ellison pleaded guilty to fraud and conspiracy, and later cooperated with prosecutors, according to the Justice Department.

    Crypto commentator Kaleo wrote on X that the series portrayed Bankman-Fried and Ellison as having been pressured and groomed by Zhao into committing their alleged crimes, while casting Zhao as the figure who orchestrated the scandal.

    "Whoever wrote this script is shameless," Kaleo added. He identifies himself as a co-founder of NFT project LedgArt.

    Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin noted in a reply on X that the show exaggerated Zhao's accent to the point of raising questions about whether the portrayal was racist.

    Meanwhile, Tigran Gambaryan, a former Binance executive and U.S. federal agent, commented on LinkedIn that the series downplayed Bankman-Fried's responsibility while portraying Zhao as a "cartoonish villain," undermining the showrunners' credibility.

    Binance co-founder Yi He criticized the series for portraying its characters as "one-dimensional" and "stereotyped," while suggesting that it shifted blame away from those responsible for FTX's collapse.

    She compared the show unfavorably with Chinese short-form drama platform Hongguo, saying Netflix "might as well be canceled.".

    But the reactions were not uniformly supportive of Zhao.

    In a post on X, OKX founder Star Xu remarked that rather than dismissing criticism as coordinated attacks by competitors, Zhao should respond with facts and evidence.

    Xu was responding to a post questioning whether accounts defending Zhao were part of a bot network.

    The eight-episode drama stars Anthony Boyle as FTX founder Sam Bankman-Fried, Julia Garner as former Alameda Research CEO Caroline Ellison and Terry Chen as Zhao.

    Netflix did not respond to a request for comment.

    In an interview published by Netflix before the series' release, Graham Moore, the show's creator and co-showrunner, said he encouraged the actors to develop fully three-dimensional characters rather than simply imitate the real-life figures they portrayed.

    Speaking to Business Insider, Moore mentioned, "I can never prove what was going on in the hearts or minds of Sam's friends when they made those decisions.".

    Moore stated he drew on extensive research into the real-life figures' backgrounds and public statements to imagine what may have driven the fractures between them.

    In a recent development, "The story we're telling is not a financial story, and it's not a crypto story. It's a deeply personal story," he added.

    While criticism of "The Altruists" has so far unfolded largely on social media, Netflix has previously faced defamation lawsuits over dramatizations of real-life events, including "Inventing Anna" and "Baby Reindeer.".

    Rachel DeLoache Williams, a former Vanity Fair photo editor, sued Netflix in 2022 over her portrayal in "Inventing Anna," a series about convicted fraudster Anna Sorokin.

    Williams alleged that the show used her real name and personal details while falsely depicting her as greedy, dishonest and disloyal, including portraying her as exploiting her friendship with Sorokin for financial gain.

    According to recent reports, the lawsuit was dismissed in February 2026 after the parties reached a settlement. Netflix and Williams' attorney reportedly confirmed the settlement in separate statements, saying, "Williams and Netflix have resolved the lawsuit.".

    According to recent reports, in 2024, Fiona Harvey, who said she inspired the character Martha in "Baby Reindeer," sued Netflix for at least $170 million. Harvey alleged that the series falsely portrayed her as a convicted stalker who had served time in prison and sexually assaulted the show's creator, Richard Gadd.

    The case is reportedly scheduled to go to trial in May 2027.

    It has been revealed that "We intend to defend this matter vigorously and to stand by Richard Gadd's right to tell his story," Netflix remarked in a statement reported by the Associated Press. She also challenged the show's claim to be based on a true story and alleged that viewers were able to identify her as the character depicted.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that the U.S.
    • Clayton noted the investigation was "ongoing" on Sunday, the day before Nvidia unveiled it had reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, a position he resigned from in part because of his relationship with Alice Huang.
    • In a recent development, alice Huang was a key figure in Megaspeed International, a cloud computing firm that operates data centers across Southeast Asia.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that the U.S. is investigating Alice Huang and her former company, Megaspeed, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said, as a report identified one of her associates as a key decision-maker at the Singapore-based company.

    Clayton noted the investigation was "ongoing" on Sunday, the day before Nvidia unveiled it had reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, a position he resigned from in part because of his relationship with Alice Huang.

    In a recent development, alice Huang was a key figure in Megaspeed International, a cloud computing firm that operates data centers across Southeast Asia. U.S. intelligence reportedly believes she is a Chinese spy.

    Recent findings suggest that "There is an investigation ongoing into her firm and into her," Clayton told ABC on Sunday, adding that, "Nvidia chips, they are the jewel. They are the absolute top that everybody wants, that's why we're focusing on this.".

    Nvidia's board unveiled Jensen Huang's return before the opening bell on Monday, saying it had "a series of discussions and meetings" with him.

    It added that it received input from senior levels of the United States government" and is confident that his reinstatement "poses no national security risk.".

    Alice Huang's associate, Chinese national Li Ming, who is now out on bail in Singapore, was "deeply involved" in Megaspeed's activities and took part in major decisions, The Wall Street Journal reported earlier on Saturday, citing people familiar with the matter.

    The Singapore charges against Li concern alleged false representations to Super Micro Computer, a U.S.-based firm with known links to chipmaker Nvidia, though Megaspeed is not named in those charges.

    Last week, the Commerce and Justice departments mentioned that the investigation into Megaspeed began in 2024 over potential export-control violations. Their joint statement said Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security and Singapore law enforcement interviewed Huang during an on-site check in June 2025.

    The Justice Department later took the lead in the criminal investigation.

    Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told CBS on Sunday that the administration was seeking answers from Nvidia about its chip sales to China, including who oversaw compliance and which levels of the firm knew about the activity.

    Recent findings suggest that separately, The Upcoming York Times reported Sunday that Alice Huang was in contact with an officer of a top Chinese intelligence agency from spring 2025 through fall 2026, citing people briefed on U.S. intelligence reports.

    Bloomberg reported last week that the Justice Department is investigating whether entities linked to Alice Huang helped smuggle Super Micro products to China.

    Li faces five charges in Singapore, including two counts of fraud by false representation, along with allegations involving the operation of a firm he controlled, unauthorized bank-account access and another company director's duties.

    Prosecutors allege he falsely told Super Micro that the manufacturer would hold and lease the servers it purchased.

    The Journal reported that Li is out on bail and that his case is ongoing. He was offered bail of S$1 million in March 2025. The Singapore charges do not name Megaspeed.

    Earlier this month, Singapore's Ministry of Home Affairs said that police had found insufficient evidence to establish that Alice Huang committed offenses related to the possible inaccurate declarations under investigation.

    According to recent reports, the ministry said she was issued a stern warning for providing information that police assessed as knowingly inaccurate and for downplaying her role at Megaspeed. It also said Singapore had not investigated her for espionage.

    Megaspeed has noted it is a "legitimate and lawful business" and that Huang left the firm in August 2025.

    According to recent reports, the scrutiny is set to intensify in Washington. Jensen Huang and the organization's general counsel, Tim Teter, have agreed to closed-door, transcribed interviews with three House committees on Dec. 1 and Dec. 2, respectively.

    The committees said they want answers about Nvidia's role in allowing Chinese actors to access advanced chips and the involvement of a potential Chinese intelligence asset.

    Industry observers note that speaking to CNBC's Squawk Box on Sunday U.S. time, Ryan Fedasiuk, a former advisor for U.S.-China Bilateral Affairs at the State Department, noted that there was "still a lot we don't know" about the case.

    He said lawmakers would likely focus on Nvidia's customer relationships and "who knew what at the firm when.".

    Fedasiuk added that there was "a very good chance" investigators would find that people at Nvidia knew their products could be used for restricted purposes. He characterized the existing evidence as containing "multiple" smoking guns.

    Industry News: Trump hosts crypto gala as his meme coin falls below $1

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • President Donald Trump on Sunday hosted his third cryptocurrency gala for top holders of his meme coin, $TRUMP, which has plummeted to below $1 a coin after reaching a high of $75 the day before Trump's second inauguration, on Jan.
    • The dinner, held at the Trump National golf club in Sterling, Virginia, comes as some Democrats say they will investigate potential conflicts of interest and accuse Trump of using the presidency to boost his personal wealth.
    • At Sunday's dinner, Trump maintained that his support for cryptocurrencies was to boost American economic competitiveness.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that U.S. President Donald Trump on Sunday hosted his third cryptocurrency gala for top holders of his meme coin, $TRUMP, which has plummeted to below $1 a coin after reaching a high of $75 the day before Trump's second inauguration, on Jan. 19, 2025.

    The dinner, held at the Trump National golf club in Sterling, Virginia, comes as some Democrats say they will investigate potential conflicts of interest and accuse Trump of using the presidency to boost his personal wealth.

    At Sunday's dinner, Trump maintained that his support for cryptocurrencies was to boost American economic competitiveness.

    "I'm doing it for the United States ... If we don't do it, China's going to do it," he told attendees, The Guardian reported. The event also featured speeches from boxing champion Floyd Mayweather, "Shark Tank" investor Kevin O'Leary and NBA champion Tristan Thompson.

    A total of 185 "wallets" met the criteria for entry to the gala, although the leaderboard on the $TRUMP coin club website listed just 130 wallets. The wallets listed on the leaderboard held $8.6 million in $TRUMP tokens, a sharp decline from the May 2025 gala, which featured 220 attendees holding a combined $148 million. Crypto billionaire Justin Sun's wallet alone held $18.5 million at the 2025 event — more than the combined holdings of this year's attendees.

    In a recent development, eligibility was based on time-weighted holdings of Trump's meme coins from Sept. 30 to Nov. 16, according to the organizer's website. The top 29 holders were invited to a VIP reception with the president, with the top four receiving an 18-karat, Trump-branded gold watch.

    More than half of the wallets that qualified for the event were linked to crypto exchanges that bar U.S.-based users, according to data gathered by consumer advocacy group Public Citizen for Reuters, suggesting they belong to foreign nationals.

    It has been revealed that the $TRUMP token has earned the Trump family at least $635 million, according to the president's June financial disclosure. Including the meme coins, the Trump family has earned $2.3 billion from its four main crypto-related businesses since the president's second term began, through to April of this year, according to a Reuters report.

    This is despite the ventures' falling value, which, according to the report, they invest little to no money in. Trump's stake in a fifth crypto-linked venture, Trump Media & Technology Group, is worth about $430 million as of Friday's close.

    Bitcoin climbed back to over $61,000 on Monday in line with the U.S. stock futures bounce, after an AI-related stock sell-off spilled over into other riskier assets last week.

    According to recent reports, bitcoin fell as low as $55,130 on Saturday, its lowest level since September 2024. The sell-off wiped out $1.8 billion in leveraged crypto positions, largely from bets on prices rising. Leveraged buyers were forced out as prices fell, then returned after the price stabilized.

    In a recent development, the world's largest cryptocurrency is still trading at less than half of its October 2025 value. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs lost $1.24 billion last week, their third week of outflows, according to SoSo Value data cited by FxPro.
