    Sources indicate that anthropic's historic IPO — the largest in U.S. history — delivered a substantial win for the tech giant and its investors. But it failed at another task: reviving animal spirits in the AI trade.

    The Nasdaq Composite closed down 2.25% amid a broader market pullback with the S&P 500 declining 2% to 7,175.

    It wasn't supposed to play out this way.

    Investors had been looking forward to the Anthropic IPO as a "clearing event" — reviving the tech sector after months of choppy trading, the Nvidia espionage scandal, and growing concerns that AI chip sales to Asia are likely to slump as Washington cracks down on potential violations of export controls.

    Industry observers note that some of those worries resurfaced Thursday as a short seller, Hunterbrook Media, alleged in a report that firmware sold by chipmaker AMD had turned up in U.S.-blacklisted companies. AMD stock closed down more than 7%. The chipmaker told CNBC it complies with U.S. law.

    Recent findings suggest that adding to the worries, the House Foreign Affairs Committee released documents showing that a subagency of the Commerce Department approved the sale of more than 879,000 AI chips to Chinese companies. That also raised the prospect of an Asia sales slowdown under stricter export controls.

    Many investors and analysts continue to express confidence in the AI trade, noting that Anthropic's successful market debut — the stock closed up 17% from its IPO price and raised more than $81 billion — bodes well for capital spending across tech.

    But investors acknowledged that this is a high-tension moment and said it's time to be more strategic about the trade.

    Dan Niles, founder of Niles Investment Management, described himself as a "circumspect bull," making the comparison to market conditions in 2022 when the big indices tanked in the back half of the year.

    Sources indicate that "You could have still made money that year. You just needed to have the right combination of longs and shorts," he said.

    Sources indicate that part of the challenge, Niles mentioned, has been a price war between the two cutting-edge frontier labs, Anthropic and OpenAI. That has posed a threat to the overall revenue and profit potential of AI and the capex going into it. Fierce competition on price is producing collective losses between the two top companies, he notes.

    Sources indicate that "The combined revenue growth for OpenAI plus Anthropic went from growing 75% sequentially in Q2 to 48% in Q3," he told CNBC. "The combined losses went from $7.9 billion to about $8.4 billion from Q2 to Q3.".

    While uncertainty is high now, some resolution may be on the horizon if a greater degree of commercial and regulatory clarity emerges over the next few months.

    Trading experts also told CNBC that the tech sector's troubles Thursday were a more serious matter than Anthropic simply siphoning capital from other parts of the market.

    "There's a reset of AI in general," mentioned JJ Kinahan, senior vice president at Cboe Global Markets.

    Investors for years have profited in tech by buying the dip, he noted, but "there's been an attitude change that [you] can't buy things blindly and they'll all go up." Nvidia's ongoing declines have shaken confidence in the buy-the-dip strategy, he said.

    According to recent reports, anthropic's next few trading days will be a key gauge of the market's strength. Friday will be a "wild card," Kinahan stated. It could be a "final flush out" for the market, or a bounce that leaves the market in "no man's land" while volatility remains elevated.

    A better gauge may be Monday, when options on Anthropic start trading, providing insight into whether retail investors will back the organization in force — providing more of a vote of confidence in the AI trade.

    "If people think we're going up [on Anthropic] they'll buy stock, but retail particularly will just buy calls," he mentioned. "There's a bigger test coming Monday.".

    For now, investors continue to sell AI-related stocks.

    Neoclouds, the generally highly indebted AI-dedicated computing providers at the outer edges of the AI trade, were down substantially Thursday, with CoreWeave closing down more than 6%.

    Hyperscalers such as Alphabet and Amazon.com, viewed as relatively defensive AI bets, also finished lower.

    One bright spot: Cybersecurity stocks continued to rally, with Palo Alto Networks and CrowdStrike both closing up. AI is finding security holes across software infrastructure, creating a scramble to patch the vulnerabilities before hackers can exploit them.

    — CNBC's Daren Fonda contributed reporting.

    #142137. Latest Update: Stuck: How a frozen housing market is hitting buyers, sellers and the economy

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1424 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest Update: Stuck: How a frozen housing market is hitting buyers, sellers and the economy

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1424 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Autumn is usually a busy time in the housing market, but not this year.
    • Buyers and sellers are moving to the sidelines, leaving those in the real estate business without much business.
    • The average rate on the popular 30-year fixed mortgage hovered around 6.60% in July, according to Mortgage News Daily.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Autumn is usually a busy time in the housing market, but not this year. A sharp spike in mortgage rates in September has pushed the already chilly real estate sector into a deep freeze.

    Buyers and sellers are moving to the sidelines, leaving those in the real estate business without much business.

    It seems like everyone is stuck.

    The average rate on the popular 30-year fixed mortgage hovered around 6.60% in July, according to Mortgage News Daily. By the start of October, it was at 7.61%, a full percentage point higher.

    "That shock, that rise of 100 basis points, is one of the fastest three-month increases we've seen in decades," mentioned Zillow CEO Jeremy Wacksman on CNBC.

    While the jump in rates exacerbated the problem, the slowdown in the housing market has been building for years. Rising home prices have pushed the dream of homeownership out of reach for a growing number of Americans. The number of active buyers nationally has been declining for six straight months and in October hit its lowest level since the aftermath of the financial crisis, according to Redfin.

    The supply of homes for sale is also low. Builders are now faced with higher costs for land, labor, materials and energy. They simply can't afford to build the cheaper homes that are currently in demand. Single-family building permits, an indicator of future construction, were down 13% in October year over year, according to the U.S. Census. And builder sentiment in November dropped to the lowest level since 2012.

    This slowdown in the entire housing ecosystem is impacting every facet of Americans' lives and livelihoods.

    "Where you live determines so much. It determines where your kids go to school. It determines the jobs that you have access to, right? It determines whether or not you're able to be close to your family," said Chen Zhao, chief economist at Redfin. "What we've seen with the housing market these past four years, with this historically low level of turnover, is that a lot of people really are stuck in their home.".

    Closed sales of existing homes fell to a 16-year low in October, according to the National Association of Realtors. Pending sales, an indicator of future closings, hit a record low on the 25-year-old index from the Realtors.

    While the pace of home price increases has slowed recently, prices are up well over 50% from pre-pandemic levels. Part of that is because homebuilding has slowed to a crawl.

    It all has Ryan Deighan, who wants to buy a home, wondering if he ever will.

    "I genuinely don't know, and that's the scary part," he stated.

    It has been revealed that deighan and his wife have been renting in Boston for six years. He is a chiropractor; she works in private equity. Even with a combined salary of more than $200,000 a year, he claims they're stuck.

    "Making what I am and what my wife makes, it just feels like we're on paper doing well, but it feels like we are still kind of fighting to put down certain amounts toward a house," Deighan stated.

    Being priced out of homeownership, he stated, is changing what he called his "checklist" of how he once pictured his future.

    "You graduate college, you find someone, you get married, you have the home with the white picket fence and the dog, and then the kids," he said. "That just looks a little different for us.".

    The numbers don't just affect would-be buyers. They are hitting sellers, too.

    Recent findings suggest that robin Welch has been living in her Cleveland-area home for more than 20 years. Her children are now grown and moved out. She would like to downsize to a condominium, but the math doesn't make sense — in part, because her current interest rate is much lower than any new rate she could get. This has been dubbed the mortgage "lock-in effect.".

    "It actually costs more money to buy less of a home," remarked Welch. "I would have to pay into an HOA, which would be another monthly expense on top of increased property taxes and increased interest rate.".

    Welch has also done upgrades to her home over the years and doesn't want to have to start doing that on another home.

    CNBC's Property Play with Diana Olick covers upcoming and evolving opportunities for the real estate investor, delivered weekly to your inbox.

    Welch is part of why the housing turnover rate, which is how often homes get new owners, has now dropped to just 3.8% a year, well below the 5% rate in the decade following the financial crisis, according to Cotality.

    In addition, the national mobility rate, which is how often people move from region to region, has been falling for two years. It now sits at 8.3%, down from 11.1% a decade ago, according to Harvard's Joint Center for Housing Studies tabulations of U.S. Census Bureau data. Mobility hit a high of nearly 18% in the late 1980s.

    Recent findings suggest that "It's largely because of the interest lock-in effect, but also because of home prices just being so high," mentioned Riordan Frost, senior research analyst at Harvard's JCHS. "Those things combined have made it hard both for existing homeowners to move and for people to get into homeownership.".

    Industry observers note that americans have nearly $35 trillion of their wealth locked up in housing, a record high, according to Cotality. But the slowdown in the housing market, Frost noted, impacts the accumulation, handover and use of that wealth. It also affects the labor market.

    "Any kind of potential job would have to really outweigh … the price of taking that mortgage with a higher rate, or the price of moving, or the price of getting into a higher rent unit," Frost noted.

    In a recent development, the wealth gap between homeowners and renters now is nothing short of massive. The most recent survey of consumer finances last year by the Federal Reserve indicated that the median homeowner net wealth is about 43 times the median renter net wealth.

    Sources indicate that "It has kind of knock-on effects for the rest of the economy. It has effects on the labor market and how good of a match we can get between employees and employers. It has an effect on education. It has an effect on just GDP growth," noted Zhao.

    When homes aren't selling and people aren't moving, those who work in that business are stuck as well. The entire housing ecosystem is churning much more slowly, and the sudden jump in mortgage rates is causing deals to fall apart.

    "Right after Labor Day, we went live with a bunch of listings. They all went under contract over the asking price," said Dana Bull, a real estate agent in the Boston suburbs. But then rates spiked.

    Industry observers note that "It was a shock to the system," Bull said. "I think all of them came back on the market. We fell out of contract." Asked if she is seeing colleagues leaving the market, she answered: "People are thinking about it. It's tough.".

    Sources indicate that the economy has lost close to 2,000 jobs in real estate and leasing over the past year and 4,400 jobs in residential construction, according to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics.

    According to recent reports, jobs in the mortgage industry have been falling since June and are down 38% since their last peak in the second quarter of 2021, according to the Mortgage Bankers Association. That was when mortgage rates were less than half what they are today.

    Shant Banosian, president of Rate and the top mortgage originator in the U.S. by dollar volume, said his business is down about 30% this past year.

    Sources indicate that "Whenever change happens swiftly, there's a slowdown," stated Banosian, who has been in the business for 23 years. "It requires more of us to go out and advise, educate and guide. So, what I experienced was I just needed to spend more time on marketing, branding, relationship building. The conversations are longer because people want more information to try to navigate this market.".

    According to recent reports, bull agrees. She mentioned her job has gotten harder as well.

    "We've done double the work this year, having homes go under contract, fall out of contract, putting them back under agreement, but definitely more negotiating," she noted. "That's sort of my plea to both buyers and sellers: We need to get back to a space where we're comfortable negotiating.".

    #142131. Latest Update: More Americans pay this Obama-era investment tax every year — how to avoid it

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (656 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest Update: More Americans pay this Obama-era investment tax every year — how to avoid it

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (656 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Every year, more Americans pay an extra tax levy on their investment gains — but there's still time to reduce or avoid that bill for 2026, experts say.
    • Sources indicate that net investment income tax, or NIIT, is a 3.8% levy on investment income once earnings exceed $200,000 for single filers or $250,000 for married couples filing jointly.
    • Unlike the federal income tax or capital gains brackets, the NIIT earnings limits don't adjust annually for inflation.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Every year, more Americans pay an extra tax levy on their investment gains — but there's still time to reduce or avoid that bill for 2026, experts say.

    Sources indicate that net investment income tax, or NIIT, is a 3.8% levy on investment income once earnings exceed $200,000 for single filers or $250,000 for married couples filing jointly. The tax was enacted in 2010 under President Barack Obama to help fund healthcare via the Affordable Care Act.

    Unlike the federal income tax or capital gains brackets, the NIIT earnings limits don't adjust annually for inflation.

    As a result, "more clients get hit every year," remarked certified financial planner Michael Walstedt, founding advisor of Reliant Wealth Advisory in Hoboken, New Jersey.

    In a recent development, roughly 5.6% of tax returns included NIIT for 2025, according to IRS data released in November for returns processed through mid-July 2026. That's up from about 3.7% for the same time frame in 2021.

    As more investors pay NIIT, here are some key things to know.

    NIIT applies when you have investment income and your earnings exceed the modified adjusted gross income, or MAGI, limits, according to certified financial planner Marianela Collado, CEO of Tobias Financial Advisors in Plantation, Florida.

    "The trick is to keep an eye on both of these numbers," said Collado, who is also a certified public accountant and member of CNBC's Financial Advisor Council.

    Industry observers note that for the NIIT earnings limit, MAGI is typically the same as adjusted gross income, or AGI. One exception would be if you have foreign income, which changes the calculation. You can find last year's AGI on line 11a of your 2025 tax return.

    Married filing jointly: $250,000.

    Married filing separately: $125,000.

    Head of household (with qualifying person): $200,000.

    Qualifying widow(er) with dependent child: $250,000.

    NIIT applies to investment income, which includes interest, dividends, annuities, royalties, certain rents, and more. It can also include capital gains from a primary home sale, for profits that exceed the IRS exclusions. The exclusion is $250,000 for single filers or $500,000 for married couples.

    Recent findings suggest that the levy stacks on top of regular income tax rates, or capital gains tax — which can be 0%, 15% or 20%, depending on earnings. That means higher earners can pay up to 23.8% on investment income, including long-term capital gains and NIIT.

    The NIIT calculation is 3.8% multiplied by the lesser of:.

    For example, if your MAGI is $30,000 above the NIIT earnings limit and you have $100,000 of investment income, you would pay 3.8% of $30,000, or $1,140.

    Alternatively, if your MAGI is $120,000 above the threshold and you have $100,000 of investment income, you would owe 3.8% of $100,000, or $3,800.

    As year-end approaches, investors should run projections to estimate their adjusted gross income, which can impact NIIT, among other tax consequences, experts say.

    If you're above the NIIT limits, you could reduce AGI by boosting pretax 401(k) deferrals or health savings account contributions, according to Collado with Tobias Financial Advisors.

    In a recent development, while employee 401(k) deferrals must happen by Dec. 31, you have until next year's tax deadline for health savings account contributions for 2026.

    You might also try to avoid selling assets before year-end, which could further boost AGI, experts say. Of course, any current-year tax moves should consider your long-term financial goals.

    Amid recent stock market volatility, investors may also consider so-called tax-loss harvesting, which uses losses to offset other portfolio gains, Walstedt with Reliant Wealth Advisory stated.

    Recent findings suggest that if your losses exceed profits, you can subtract up to $3,000 from regular income. After that, you can carry remaining losses into future tax years.

    However, if you're planning to reinvest the sale proceeds, you need to know the "wash sale rule," which blocks the tax-loss harvesting tax break for buying a "substantially identical" asset within 30 days before or after the sale.

    #142126. Latest Update: Tokenized stocks face pushback as NYSE, Nasdaq pivot for a upcoming market

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1055 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest Update: Tokenized stocks face pushback as NYSE, Nasdaq pivot for a upcoming market

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1055 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • OKXICE, a trading platform for tokenized securities jointly operated by Intercontinental Exchange and crypto exchange OKX, is set to debut Monday despite objections from 90% of the companies whose stocks it initially proposed to list.
    • Of the 62 companies whose shares OKXICE first sought to trade, 56 objected to having their shares tokenized and traded on the platform, according to a review of public notices posted between Oct.
    • The high objection rate may reflect companies' lack of readiness to have blockchain-based representations of their shares traded on a latest third-party platform like OKXICE, rather than broad resistance to tokenization.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    OKXICE, a trading platform for tokenized securities jointly operated by Intercontinental Exchange and crypto exchange OKX, is set to debut Monday despite objections from 90% of the companies whose stocks it initially proposed to list.

    Of the 62 companies whose shares OKXICE first sought to trade, 56 objected to having their shares tokenized and traded on the platform, according to a review of public notices posted between Oct. 4 and Nov. 5. By last week, even more companies had objected, including those not on the original roster.

    The high objection rate may reflect companies' lack of readiness to have blockchain-based representations of their shares traded on a latest third-party platform like OKXICE, rather than broad resistance to tokenization.

    People involved in talks with some of the companies say a 30-day objection window left them little time to react and decide if they were ready to participate.

    Industry observers note that "The shift to a 24/7 global marketplace is revolutionary and transformational for our market structure," Andrew Cuomo, co-chair of OKXICE, told CNBC. "The majority of companies aren't familiar with [tokenization] and haven't had a chance to understand it and the consequences.".

    "Logic dictates that many companies were going to be cautious before they understood what the system would do," added Cuomo, who served 10 years as governor of Newly introduced York until 2021. "What you're seeing now is the more the companies learn about 24/7 global access, the more receptive they are.".

    At launch, tokenized shares of Coinbase, Robinhood, Strategy, Circle, Securitize and BitGo will be available to trade on the platform, OKXICE disclosed in a public notice. OKXICE has confirmed 113 assets, including exchange-traded funds and products, going live on a rolling basis. Since its initial pre-launch announcement on Nov. 11, OKXICE noted it's seen further interest from different issuers and Fidelity Investments, Direxion, eToro, Strive and Vida Global are now participating.

    The 30-day opt-out window is a requirement of the SEC's so-called Innovation Exemption, which took effect in September and temporarily permits the trading of certain tokenized stocks. Under the exemption, trading platforms must notify the underlying issuers and give them an opportunity to object. Any issuer who objects blocks its shares from being tokenized.

    "We've gotten a lot of feedback that the reason why you've seen this high number of rejections of tokenizing equity is because it was a 30-day window," Seth Ginns, chief investment officer at Franklin Templeton's crypto arm, told CNBC at the Digital Assets Forum in Fresh York earlier this month. Many issuers were open to exploring the idea but were hesitant to move forward amid competing priorities, he said.

    According to recent reports, "[They're] saying it's earnings season, there was the midterms, there's a lot going on during this 30-day window. Give us some time, we want to learn about it, we're not closed to the idea we're just closed to rushing into it right now," Ginns added.

    Ran Grushkowsky, CEO of MassPay, a global payout platform, mentioned several of his firm's clients were among the initial targets and shared that their concern was less about the concept of tokenization and more about how 24/7 trading could affect stock value and investor relations strategies, particularly around the timing of corporate announcements.

    Recent findings suggest that "It's more [about] what's going to be the effect, how is it going to actually drive the value of the stock," he noted. "A lot of the strategy that happens around investors relations has to do with scheduling and when you announce certain things and so how do you do it when your stock is being traded 24/7?".

    "The executives were actually quite excited about this new innovation and potentially getting more interest into the stock. It was really from the [investor relations] side that they received push back," and heard "let's hold off," Grushkowsky added.

    The lack of awareness may even extend to executives overseeing digital asset initiatives, suggesting that some rejections stem from internal communication gaps and unfamiliarity with the process, according to Securitize CEO Carlos Domingo, whose manufacturer is one of the first being listed on OKX. Securitize is also the tokenization partner for OKX.

    "We've talked to some of the issuers that have opted out [where] the head of digital assets doesn't even know who in the company rejected them," he said. "This is a consequence of, first, the novelty of the process and of these venues, and second, the lack of understanding of what they're being notified to do.".

    Despite the initial pushback, Domingo expects more issuers to participate as companies become more familiar with the model, noting that some regulated trading venues can operate without issuer consent.

    According to recent reports, firm objections raise a separate question about which of the different tokenization models will prove most attractive. The main alternative to the OKXICE model is an issuer-led approach that integrates blockchain-based shares into existing regulated market infrastructures, with issuers retaining greater control over the process.

    Bullish, a digital asset platform, is pursuing an example of this model through its partnership with Equiniti, the transfer-agent business it's acquiring for $4 billion.

    Nasdaq's planned launch of an issuer-centric tokenized equities model in partnership with Kraken parent Payward in the second quarter of next year could offer a test of that framework and whether companies are more willing to embrace tokenization under a different structure.

    According to recent reports, nasdaq and the Fresh York Stock Exchange, owned by Intercontinental, and others are responding to a structural shift in how securities are issued, traded and settled. Tokenization has become attractive to institutions and investors because it enables round the clock stock trading, shortened settlement times, fractional ownership and eases the use of securities as collateral.

    In a recent development, for the exchanges, it presents a way to keep control of trading and market infrastructure as crypto-native, blockchain-based venues seek to bring traditional financial assets on to blockchain. It's a long way off before it becomes a meaningful revenue driver, however, according to Clear Street analyst Owen Lau.

    According to recent reports, "It increases the [total addressable market], that's the number one thing," Lau said. "In the near term, there may not be enough of an incremental revenue opportunity, but the trend is there. The trend is to tokenize equities, the trend is to facilitate 24/7 trading.".

    CrowdStrike to buy Zscaler in $44 billion deal as AI supercharges cyberattacks

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (442 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • CrowdStrike aims to buy Zscaler for $43.9 billion in an all-stock deal that combines two significant security businesses at a time when artificial intelligence is supercharging attacks.
    • Shares of CrowdStrike dropped roughly 5% in early trading Monday, while Zscaler surged more than 20%.
    • According to recent reports, the deal is expected to close in the second half of CrowdStrike's fiscal year 2028.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    CrowdStrike aims to buy Zscaler for $43.9 billion in an all-stock deal that combines two significant security businesses at a time when artificial intelligence is supercharging attacks.

    Shares of CrowdStrike dropped roughly 5% in early trading Monday, while Zscaler surged more than 20%.

    According to recent reports, the deal is expected to close in the second half of CrowdStrike's fiscal year 2028. Under the agreement, Zscaler shareholders will receive 1.135 CrowdStrike shares for each share.

    CrowdStrike's acquisition pushes the Austin-based cyber vendor into the network security market and comes amid a massive year for cybersecurity dealmaking in the wake of high-profile hacks like Hugging Face.

    "With Zscaler, we're building cybersecurity's operating system: a single control plane to deploy AI, control AI, and enable any agentic application to run safely," CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz said in a statement. "We see a path to become the largest AI safety and security manufacturer the world has ever seen.".

    Recent outages affecting Microsoft, the Federal Aviation Administration and JPMorgan Chase have sparked anxiety as businesses accelerate software patching and upgrades to aging systems in an effort to prevent bad actors from exploiting software vulnerabilities with AI.

    CrowdStrike has been a major beneficiary of skyrocketing demand for AI security, with shares soaring about 80% this year as of Monday's open. Zscaler shares are up about 5% year to date after Monday's surge. Their combined market value exceeded $265 billion as of Friday's close, behind market leader Palo Alto Networks at $282 billion.

    The deal marks CrowdStrike's biggest acquisition to date and is among the largest in the sector as businesses consolidate and ramp up defenses to fend off AI-powered attacks.

    Last year, Google unveiled intends to acquire Wiz for $32 billion. In 2024 Cisco shelled about $28 billion for Splunk. Competitor Palo Alto Networks has also spent billions on several cyber and AI businesses, including startup Applied Compute and a $25 billion deal for CyberArk, which it closed earlier this year.

    Analysts view the Zscaler deal as a major AI security opportunity, allowing CrowdStrike to capture more customer security spending and close a significant gap with Palo Alto.

    "The addition of ZS to CRWD's platform could bring more breadth in an era of vendor consolidation and, more importantly, network security to position the company more effectively for rising demand for AI Sovereignty," wrote analysts at JPMorgan.

    CrowdStrike on Monday also reported better-than-expected fiscal third-quarter results, including earnings of 34 cents per share on $1.58 billion in revenue. That topped the 31 cents per share on $1.53 billion in revenue forecast by LSEG.

    Zscaler's fiscal first-quarter earnings, also released on Monday, likewise surpassed estimates.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Cathie Wood was a major buyer of Anthropic following its debut Thursday on the Nasdaq, adding shares in all her major funds.
    • Wood's firm, which already owned private shares of the artificial intelligence company in its Ark Venture Fund leading up to the initial public offering, bought $90.8 million worth of Anthropic in six funds, according to a trade notification from the firm.
    • "We've owned Anthropic since early '23," Wood told CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Friday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Cathie Wood was a major buyer of Anthropic following its debut Thursday on the Nasdaq, adding shares in all her major funds.

    Wood's firm, which already owned private shares of the artificial intelligence company in its Ark Venture Fund leading up to the initial public offering, bought $90.8 million worth of Anthropic in six funds, according to a trade notification from the firm.

    "We've owned Anthropic since early '23," Wood told CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Friday. "It's our best performing equity by far in ARKVX, our venture fund. ... Our confidence has grown with time as it really took over the enterprise" AI business.

    It has been revealed that anthropic shares jumped 17% in their first day, but closed well off the highs of the session and were headed for sizable losses Friday. The Nasdaq, which was expected to get a boost from a major IPO reviving enthusiasm about the technology trade, fell by 2% on Thursday.

    Sources indicate that "We're climbing a wall of worry," noted Wood. "Everybody is worried about AI hype and the political situation after the election, but I think we'll look back and say, OK this is more like the '80s and '90s, climbing a wall of worry you know with bricks much like what we have today: inflation, interest rates, wars, latest technologies and so forth so quite optimistic here.".

    Industry observers note that the Anthropic stakes are relatively small across the funds, but Wood typically will buy shares in companies she likes steadily during long stretches. Wood said she is "averaging down" with her purchases of Anthropic.

    Recent findings suggest that in her $6.1 billion Ark Innovation ETF, Anthropic is a 0.3% stake. The biggest holdings in that fund are Tesla and SpaceX, representing more than 21% of the fund together.

    Ark Innovation, which retail investors piled into during the pandemic as it gained about 150% in 2020, tumbled the subsequent next two years, losing 67% in 2022 alone. Wood's following was dented after the big losses.

    The fund had a comeback stretch as the bull market revved back up from 2023 to 2025, but has fallen on hard times again this year, down more than 10% in 2026. The S&P 500 is up 4.8% this year.

    Wood dismissed comparisons of today's environment to the dot-com bubble.

    In a recent development, "Back then if an Anthropic had gone public, it probably would have gone up threefold the first day," she stated. "That's how crazy things were.".

    SpaceX sued by Oregon and Virginia over AI deepfake porn, Grok safety claims

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (721 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Lawsuits against Elon Musk's SpaceX are stacking up, with Virginia and Oregon becoming the first states to sue the manufacturer over issues with its Grok AI image generator.
    • Versions of Grok and SpaceX's social network X have enabled users to generate and distribute explicit deepfakes based on real photos or videos of children and other people who did not consent, according to research by the Internet Watch Foundation, the Center for Countering Digital Hate and others.
    • In separate complaints submitted to state courts as of Monday morning, Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield and Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones argued that SpaceX failed to put safeguards in place to stop Grok and X customers from making and sharing harmful deepfake images, especially alleged AI-generated child sexual abuse material.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Lawsuits against Elon Musk's SpaceX are stacking up, with Virginia and Oregon becoming the first states to sue the manufacturer over issues with its Grok AI image generator.

    Versions of Grok and SpaceX's social network X have enabled users to generate and distribute explicit deepfakes based on real photos or videos of children and other people who did not consent, according to research by the Internet Watch Foundation, the Center for Countering Digital Hate and others.

    In separate complaints submitted to state courts as of Monday morning, Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield and Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones argued that SpaceX failed to put safeguards in place to stop Grok and X customers from making and sharing harmful deepfake images, especially alleged AI-generated child sexual abuse material.

    It has been revealed that the complaints also allege that SpaceX has falsely represented its AI apps and social network (Grok and X) as generally safe, which the states see as a violation of Virginia's Consumer Protection Act or Oregon's Unlawful Trade Practices Act. The matter is particularly concerning because X allows minors 13 and older to access its content.

    Rayfield and Jones both noted in their complaints that harms caused by non-consensual, sexualized images go beyond the victims depicted in the images.

    According to recent reports, "This content can cause fear, distress, and anxiety in those who are unwillingly exposed to the content," Jones wrote. Rayfield wrote that such conduct "erodes vital norms regarding consent and privacy and trivializes sexual imagery, abuse, and exploitation.".

    In a statement emailed to CNBC by a spokesperson for SpaceXSI, and posted on the firm's @Safety account on X, the company stated, "When someone tries to break our safeguards and generate this content, we take appropriate measures, including actioning accounts and notifying law enforcement. Attempting to create this material is a serious crime, and the individuals who do it should be prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law. We will continue to work with the authorities via all available means to pursue these bad actors.".

    At an NYC Council hearing in October, a SpaceX AI policy leader, Gabriela Castillo Madrid, mentioned the company had appropriate "safeguards" and "strict controls" in place around its AI products.

    SpaceX was already facing multiple Grok- and X-related lawsuits, and government probes around the world, including by authorities in the U.K., Spain, Ireland, France and the state of California.

    Industry observers note that in private-sector lawsuits filed against SpaceX in the U.S. concerning Grok and AI-generated, explicit images, litigation is still in early stages and is tracked by The Center for Internet Technology Addiction.

    According to recent reports, when the city of Baltimore sued xAI, now owned and operated by SpaceX, the tech giant argued that under Section 230, they were not liable for unwanted images. Section 230 is a federal law that largely shields online platforms from liability for customers' content.

    Recent findings suggest that spaceX also sued a user in a federal court in the Northern District of Texas for breach of contract after he allegedly used Grok to create and distribute deepfake explicit images, including depictions of minors. Lawyers for Musk's tech giant argued that Grok should be seen as "a neutral tool, subject to user control," and that any image generation "is the result of the user's prompts and directions.".

    The new state suits add to legal pressure on SpaceX. Both Virginia and Oregon are seeking injunctions, civil penalties, disgorgement and legal costs, while Virginia is also seeking restitution for consumers from Musk's company.

    Oregon submitted its complaint to the Multnomah County Circuit Court on Sunday evening, and Virginia submitted its complaint to the City of Richmond Circuit Court Monday morning. As of early Monday, the suits were pending the courts' acceptance.

    In a recent development, state attorneys general have recently succeeded in compelling U.S. social media companies to change their products and pay for alleged past harms.

    Sources indicate that in August, for example, Meta settled a major federal case centered on allegations that the social media giant misrepresented the level of child mental health problems caused by its apps, Facebook and Instagram. Without admitting to wrongdoing, Meta agreed to pay states around $17 billion over a 10-year period and to make app changes that experts believe will help keep children safer online.

    As Anthropic shares tank, investors scramble to hedge. It could be very expensive

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, as Anthropic shares tumble toward their IPO price of $83, investors are looking for ways to hedge.
    • If Anthropic breaks its IPO price, it will represent a 27% decline from Thursday's intraday high of $113.
    • Options traders are also looking at how SpaceX traded in the days following its offering for clues on how options might price.

    According to recent reports, as Anthropic shares tumble toward their IPO price of $83, investors are looking for ways to hedge. Unfortunately, they may have to wait until Monday, when options on the AI giant are expected to list.

    If Anthropic breaks its IPO price, it will represent a 27% decline from Thursday's intraday high of $113. The wild price swings offer clues on how expensive it might be to buy protection on the new tech giant once options begin trading.A 20% intraday move points to an implied volatility somewhere between 100 and 150 for Anthropic options, according to estimates from single-stock market-makers on the Cboe trading floor in Chicago.

    Options traders are also looking at how SpaceX traded in the days following its offering for clues on how options might price.

    According to recent reports, implied volatility in SpaceX started at 116, but that didn't deter options traders big and small from piling into the contracts tracking the stock, with about 1.7 million contracts traded on the first day for a total options premium of about $2.5 billion. Far out-of-the-money call contracts were some of the most popular trades as the stock soared 40% in its first three sessions.One key difference between now and then? Anthropic is trading against the backdrop of S&P 500 volatility close to 30, compared to 17.3 when SpaceX debuted. "I expect ANT options to be super active," stated Tom Sosnoff, co-founder of the trading platforms ThinkOrSwim and TastyTrade. "I expect heavy options volume."One thing Anthropic and SpaceX have in common is heavy retail involvement in both IPOs, with retail brokerages receiving a 20% allocation from SpaceX and reports pointing to between a 15-20% allocation from Anthropic on Thursday. "Round one of the Anthropic IPO easily goes to the individual investor," Sosnoff added. "Retail participants bailed early at the best prices of the day while institutional investors paid up to top off their underwhelming allocations. I believe retail was aggressively reloading in the mid-90s."Further signs of retail demand will become evident when options likely begin trading on Monday. One thing to watch: the spread between out-of-the-money call and put contracts, which was heavily skewed toward calls in the case of SpaceX. "I would be careful comparing Anthropic to SpaceX," said Dennis Davitt, CIO and Co-Founder of Millbank Dartmoor Portsmouth. "From a market-structure perspective, the two are dramatically different. The availability and cost of borrowing will be different, the companies are at very different stages of maturity, and SpaceX has allowed employees to monetize portions of their holdings over time. All of those factors matter when pricing options.".

    Shares of Nvidia surged 30% after Jensen Huang was reinstated as CEO of the firm.

    In a recent development, nvidia's surge and Huang's reinstatement follow a more than 40% slump in the stock over the past month, as Huang was ousted as CEO of the company he founded after he admitted to having an extramarital affair with a woman U.S. intelligence reportedly believes to be a Chinese spy.

    Industry observers note that the Nasdaq slid 10% last week and opened more than 6% higher Monday. All three major averages ended last week in correction territory, and the Nasdaq turned negative for 2026. Tech stocks remain rocky as investors remain nervous about the valuation of some AI companies and business models.

    Stocks of Big Tech companies and other stocks related to the AI trade also saw a lift Monday after the Nvidia news.

    Alphabet stock surged 6%, while Meta added more than 5%, Amazon was up nearly 5% and Microsoft jumped 4%. SpaceX climbed 9% and AMD added over 8.5%.

    Neoclouds, which have seen a particularly choppy few months, surged. Nebius was up over 30%, CoreWeave 28% and Iren 28%.

    Anthropic shares were flat after a brief premarket surge, in its third day of trading following its initial public offering on Thursday.

    Sources indicate that anthropic raised a record $93.5 billion in its IPO. The stock gained 17% in its debut on Thursday, before closing down 8.5% on Friday.

    #142092. ‘This establishes a bottom’: Jensen Huang’s return seen as likely to stop market sell-off, for now

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (779 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    ‘This establishes a bottom’: Jensen Huang’s return seen as likely to stop market sell-off, for now

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (779 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that the major averages of U.S.
    • In a recent development, the relief rally came after the Dow Jones Industrial Average, S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite ended Friday's session in correction territory.
    • Recent findings suggest that that sell-off may be over — at least temporarily — according to Wall Street experts.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that the major averages of U.S. equities surged on Monday after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, giving investors some hope that the relentless selling pressure seen last week may subside — at least temporarily.

    In a recent development, the relief rally came after the Dow Jones Industrial Average, S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite ended Friday's session in correction territory. The S&P alone tumbled more than 9% after Huang's departure from the chipmaker was initially announced on Nov. 12 through Friday.

    Recent findings suggest that that sell-off may be over — at least temporarily — according to Wall Street experts. But key questions linger around Nvidia and the artificial intelligence trade that has carried the bull market.

    In a recent development, "I think the AI trade is back on," remarked Mark Gibbens, founder of Gibbens Capital Management. "I certainly believe this establishes a bottom and a floor in the AI trade and the recent market weakness.".

    According to recent reports, he added that the news likely doesn't alleviate all concerns that have driven recent declines, including worries about data center approvals after the midterms and fears that the capital expenditures cycle may have peaked. But Gibbens thinks the "keystone" role that Nvidia plays in both financing the AI build-out and the technology's supply chain means a more stable picture of the chipmaker creates a brighter view of the overall market than before.

    An encouraging sign that the correction may be over came even before Nvidia's Monday announcement, according to Art Hogan, chief market strategist at B. Riley Wealth Management. He remarked Friday's selling, which was indiscriminate and affected sectors beyond just AI-exposed companies, showed a bottom may have been building.

    Sources indicate that "Sometimes you just hit that crescendo where you know the market gets oversold, and I would argue that we'd be higher today, even without the Nvidia news," he said. Indeed, futures tied to the major stock indexes were broadly higher on Sunday night, before any news regarding Huang's return. "So I think that sort of signals we've likely found a place where we priced in, at least the near term, as much of the bad news that was giving markets jitters over the course of the last several weeks.".

    According to recent reports, strengthening the case for a bottom was that the technology sector's forward earnings valuation was cheaper than that of consumer staples, Hogan mentioned. The S&P 500 consumer staples sector trades at a 20.5 multiple, per FactSet. Tech, meanwhile, trades at 16.3 times forward earnings. Hogan said that discrepancy doesn't square with the earnings outlook for the former sector.

    Industry observers note that jay Woods, chief market strategist at Freedom Capital Markets, noted Huang's return created a relief rally for a market that was oversold. But he's not sure the headline alone can get the market out of its funk.

    Industry observers note that "I think the rally will probably fizzle out because now people will pull back and still have the same questions we had before he was replaced," Woods said. Those questions will likely play out in congressional hearings, he speculated. "The market needed this jolt to get us back on our feet, but it is still a counter trend rally in an otherwise near-term downtrend.".

    Woods, though, remarked that the lows for the year are likely in, thanks to Friday's wash-out that spread to all sectors beyond those dependent on Nvidia's role in AI.

    While investors celebrated Huang's return, the sell-off that accelerated after his departure started before worries about his position even began. That stemmed from concerns about financing the build-out, data center approvals after Democratic wins in the midterm elections and worries that hyperscaler capex may have already peaked or is about to.

    That's why Peter Boockvar, CIO at One Point BFG Wealth Partners, is still nervous about the "picks and shovels" companies involved in the AI trade, a group he notes includes Nvidia.

    It has been revealed that "We should enjoy this rally, and maybe it lasts a bit, but I think that picks and shovels trade is going to be solely dependent on what that rate of capex spend is going to be," he said. "That at the end of the day is the story that those companies are going to have to deal with outside of bounces like we're seeing now.".

    Traders at Goldman Sachs put it more succinctly.

    "Not sure yet whether good or bad that the fate of the market is almost equal to the fate of one person. But hey... We are not picky here," they said.

    — CNBC's Michelle Fox and Deena Zaidi contributed reporting.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    As stocks continue their tech-driven sell-off, prediction markets traders are seeing a bleaker outlook for the remainder of the year.

    It has been revealed that on platform Kalshi, speculators place just 6% odds that the S&P 500 will cross 8,000 in 2026. On Oct. 13, those odds were as high as 72%.

    Contracts ask traders if the S&P 500 will go above various levels in 2026, and they're resolved using data from S&P Dow Jones Indices.

    According to recent reports, on Friday, the Nasdaq Composite turned negative for the year as investors continued to dump tech stocks, primarily those with exposure to the artificial intelligence build-out. The Dow Jones Industrial Average and the S&P 500 fell into correction territory, too.

    The S&P 500 has slashed its year-to-date gain to just over 2%.

    The Stock Trader's Almanac in a Thursday note broadly agreed that the hopes for a December rally are fading, with the caveat that a "Santa rally" could still appear at the end of the year.

    "The market is under pressure and more downside can't be ruled out," the note said.

    Industry observers note that the Stock Trader's Almanac sees 2026 following the year-end pattern of 2018, when the Federal Reserve was in a tightening cycle in a midterm year. The Fed is widely expected to hike rates at its December meeting.

    In that scenario, the Stock Trader's Almanac thinks more churn is to come. "The low is more likely in mid- to late December than this week.".

    #142085. Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO. Stock skyrockets 33%

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (973 w)
    📖 Baca
    Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

    Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO. Stock skyrockets 33%

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (973 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Nvidia on Monday unveiled Jensen Huang has been reinstated as CEO, effective immediately, a dramatic twist in a scandal that hammered the chipmaker's stock price and rocked the tech and artificial intelligence industries.
    • In a recent development, the board of directors said it unanimously voted to reinstate Huang following "a series of discussions and meetings" with him.
    • President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday that he had been speaking to Nvidia's board "directly and indirectly," and that Huang "did nothing wrong." Trump stated he talked to Huang on Sunday and asked him to promise to "work hard.".
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Nvidia on Monday unveiled Jensen Huang has been reinstated as CEO, effective immediately, a dramatic twist in a scandal that hammered the chipmaker's stock price and rocked the tech and artificial intelligence industries.

    In a recent development, the board of directors said it unanimously voted to reinstate Huang following "a series of discussions and meetings" with him. The board added that it "received input from senior levels of the United States government" and that it is confident Huang's reinstatement "poses no national security risk.".

    President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday that he had been speaking to Nvidia's board "directly and indirectly," and that Huang "did nothing wrong." Trump stated he talked to Huang on Sunday and asked him to promise to "work hard.".

    Huang resigned from his role as chief executive earlier this month after a series of shocking reports about multiple extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. The Upcoming York Times reported on Sunday that the woman, Alice Huang, was in contact with an officer of China's Ministry of State Security during at least part of the time that she was engaging in a relationship with Huang.

    Sources indicate that shares of Nvidia surged 33% following Huang's reinstatement. The stock had shed nearly 33% from the time Huang admitted to an extramarital affair on Nov. 8. The stock closed at $186.64 on Nov.6.

    In a recent development, "I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a fresh industrial revolution," Huang noted in a statement. "I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the NVIDIA Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process.".

    Senior government officials briefed Nvidia's board late last week and communicated that no national security laws were violated, according to sources familiar with the discussion who asked to remain anonymous because they were not authorized to speak publicly. That enhancement prompted the board to reach out to Huang, the people said.

    Huang and the board held their first conversations since his ouster on Saturday, and the group determined he would return as CEO during a second meeting on Sunday, the people said. Nvidia's cratering stock price played a role in accelerating those conversations.

    It has been revealed that trump celebrated Huang's return to Nvidia on Monday, writing in a post on his social media site that the board made "the correct and proper decision" to reinstate him. Trump said the U.S. needs Huang's leadership to "ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy.".

    He reiterated that the U.S. government has "no reason to believe" Huang's return poses a risk to national security, and that it "does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.".

    "On a personal note, I have gotten to know Jensen, and he is a Great Patriot and National Treasure," Trump wrote.

    Sources indicate that several tech industry leaders, including Elon Musk, CEO of SpaceX, Gavin Baker, managing partner and chief investment officer at Atreides Management, and Brad Gerstner, Altimeter Capital CEO, had been actively lobbying for Huang's return. Musk wrote in a post on X on Monday that the board's "mistake has been corrected.".

    Nvidia did not immediately respond to CNBC's request for comment.

    Sources indicate that for weeks following Huang's ouster, the organization's board maintained that it was not considering Huang's reinstatement. It appointed Colette Kress, Nvidia's chief financial officer, as the chipmaker's interim CEO, who reiterated that position in an interview with CNBC following Huang's exit. Kress will continue to serve as Nvidia's CFO, according to a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

    Nvidia's board formed an independent committee and hired the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct an investigation into Huang and whether organization secrets or national security were compromised. The board stated Monday that "the committee's investigation will proceed to conclusion" and that Huang is "committed to cooperating with it.".

    "The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," Nvidia's board chair, Harvey Jones, remarked in a statement. "We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Company.".

    Even with Huang back at the helm, Nvidia is facing increased scrutiny over its chip sales in Southeast Asia and China.

    Sources indicate that lawmakers have been preparing for investigations into how Huang's affair with the alleged spy may have damaged U.S. AI dominance, influenced his positions on export controls, and impacted his close relationships with Trump and his Cabinet. Huang has been one of the loudest voices opposing strict export controls on advanced chips.

    "The reckless decision to bring Jensen Huang back as CEO does not change the fact that Mr. Huang, NVIDIA executives, and the company's board still owe Congress answers about the company's compliance with U.S. export controls," Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., stated in a statement Monday.

    Sources indicate that huang is due for a closed-door transcribed interview with the House Foreign Affairs panel and two other committees on Dec. 1. Nvidia's general counsel, Tim Teter, is scheduled to appear before the panels on Dec. 2. Those dates were set before Huang's return, and John Fisher, who represents Huang, did not comment on whether there are any changes in his plans to testify.

    "Americans deserve answers about what NVIDIA and the Trump administration knew, when they knew it, and whether sufficient steps were taken to prevent sensitive technology from falling into the wrong hands," Sen. Andy Kim, D-N.J., wrote in a post on X on Monday.

    #142082. Fantasy Football Stock Report: Jonah Coleman looking like league-winning back after 3-TD performance in Week 11

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1884 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy 📈 Bullish 🌐 Yahoo ↗ Open Full Page

    Fantasy Football Stock Report: Jonah Coleman looking like league-winning back after 3-TD performance in Week 11

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1884 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Yahoo

    ⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • As I write this on Sunday night, 12 of 13 Week 11 games are in the books (with Monday night remaining) and the fantasy football season is now past the halfway point.
    • Industry observers note that with that in mind, I've compiled another full fantasy stock report.
    • In a recent development, barring something extraordinary, Jonah Coleman has locked down the award for Waiver Wire Pickup of the Year.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    As I write this on Sunday night, 12 of 13 Week 11 games are in the books (with Monday night remaining) and the fantasy football season is now past the halfway point. Still, things are changing every week. Promising improvements. Concerning trends. Performances that change our early outlook on players and teams. As always, some of these shifting perspectives will have permanent ramifications in fantasy.

    Industry observers note that with that in mind, I've compiled another full fantasy stock report. These are the most notable risers and fallers heading into Week 12.

    In a recent development, barring something extraordinary, Jonah Coleman has locked down the award for Waiver Wire Pickup of the Year. He scored a monster 32.9 fantasy points on Sunday, taking 24 carries for 111 yards and three touchdowns while adding four catches for 18 yards. That makes three straight games with 15+ touches and more touches in every successive game since returning from injury in Week 7. He's become a legitimate bell-cow back for Denver, a winning team with a strong defense, and has an excellent schedule down the stretch as well. There's no longer a question on whether Coleman will remain a weekly fantasy starter — now the question is whether he'll be a high-end RB2 or a low-end RB1 for the rest of the season. Honestly, with the volume he's accumulated and the impact he's had with that volume, I'd lean towards the latter. If you added him earlier this season — or were smart enough to draft and hold him — congratulations. You got a league-winner.

    In Travis Etienne Jr.'s first week back from injury, the usage split with Audric Estimé and Alvin Kamara was extremely discouraging. He saw just eight carries to Estimé's seven and was matched at three catches by Kamara, while playing just 34.4% of the snaps. However, things changed dramatically this past Sunday against the Bears. Etienne shouldered 14 carries, while no other running back had more than one, and managed 5.4 yards per carry for a total of 76 yards.

    Now, he was mostly uninvolved as a receiver and Kamara vultured another touchdown from the goal line, so it seems like Etienne's upside will still be capped much lower than we might have hoped when Newly introduced Orleans signed him in the offseason. But, at the very least, he's back to being the RB1 for the team. And he'll have several much easier matchups than Jeffery Simmons and the Bears in the near future, including the Panthers in Week 14 and the Falcons in the fantasy championship. He's probably a borderline RB2 moving forward, but that's legitimately the best outlook he's had since Week 1.

    A week ago, Chris Olave took the biggest stock dip of the 2026 season, when he was massively outproduced by rookie Jordyn Tyson and finished with just three catches for 30 yards on four targets against the Panthers. The dip didn't last long. Against the Bears on Sunday, Olave saw 15 targets and caught nine of them for 102 yards. It was his seventh game of the season with double-digit targets and his most catches since Week 3 and most yards since Week 4.

    Industry observers note that incidentally, it was Tyson who disappeared in this one (with just one catch on two targets) and Devaughn Vele who stepped up in his stead (with seven catches on seven targets). Ultimately, the most reasonable takeaway here is that Olave is still, and should continue to remain, the Fresh Orleans WR1, despite the spotty breakout from Tyson. Poor play from Tyler Shough and a mixed set of matchups down the road keep Olave from fantasy WR1 territory — as evidenced by his four-game stretch without a touchdown — but reclaiming his spot atop the pecking order should lock Olave back in as a WR2 for the remainder of the season.

    As odd as it may be, there's a viable fantasy running back behind Derrick Henry right now. Justice Hill took six carries for 69 yards and a touchdown on Sunday, while adding four catches for 27 yards on five targets. It was his second game in the last three weeks with 15+ fantasy points, bringing his average over that span to 12.9 per game, and he's now logged 3+ catches in six straight games. Hill has been extremely explosive all year and is clearly the preferred pass-catcher out of the backfield. And with Jacoby Brissett at quarterback for the foreseeable future, we can expect the Ravens to trail more and throw more than they ever would with Lamar Jackson. Both are good news for Hill, who's shaping up as a weekly FLEX consideration. He won't be an RB2 with any sort of reliability as long as Henry is leading the backfield, but he's a fantasy contributor at a thin and ever thinner position.

    Finally, after a nine-week stretch with fewer than 11 fantasy points every single week, Ladd McConkey returned to relevance in Week 11. He caught five passes on eight targets, and while he only managed 37 yards, he scored two touchdowns on the day, doubling his season total entering the weekend. It was a season high in targets and his most catches since Week 1, indicating that he's finally back to being fully healthy and involved as Los Angeles seemingly continues to turn its offense around (the Chargers have scored more points in three successive games, culminating in a season-high 24 on Sunday).

    According to recent reports, obviously there were high expectations for McConkey and this offense entering the season, which has painted their struggles in an even darker shadow. But if McConkey's 18.2 fantasy points were an indication of a late-season resurgence, it's possible he'll finally return a little bit on the investment managers made back in the summer. Justin Herbert did end up in concussion protocol after this game, so hopefully he clears that protocol by next weekend ... especially given the matchup with the Patriots, who have one of the softest defenses for wide receivers this season. McConkey has easy WR2 potential in that contest, as long as everyone is healthy.

    While the stock isn't cratering on Luther Burden III, given how consistently great he had been entering the Week 10 bye, that consistency is what made Sunday's disappearance so troubling. After three straight games with a touchdown, four straight with double-digit fantasy points and seven straight with at least four catches, Burden logged just two receptions for 10 yards on three targets in Week 11 (and added one rush for three yards). He also ran only 17 routes (fewer than Kalif Raymond's 20) and it felt worryingly like the first month of the season, when the Bears receiving corps was a convoluted mess and Burden was "just fine.".

    Industry observers note that also, it's not like the Bears were blowing the Saints out for the majority of the game, which might have explained the lower volume, they were just intent on spreading the ball around ... a lot. All this said, none of the Bears receivers leapfrogged Burden in any sort of meaningful way — Rome Odunze had just four catches, Raymond had one and no one had 60 receiving yards — so this can likely be classified as a fluke more than anything. Still, it was a reminder that this is an unusual offense with a prominent ground game, a ton of weapons and no real "alpha WR1." Burden should be fine down the stretch, at least as a fantasy WR2, but likely will not be a bona fide No. 1 with occasional duds like this.

    Recent findings suggest that after an incredible two-month stretch to start the season, in which he was the RB12 with 16 fantasy points per game, Jaylen Warren has now scored fewer than seven fantasy points in back-to-back weeks. After managing just 15 yards on seven carries in Week 10 (but catching five passes for 26 yards to sort of salvage the week), Warren had just 28 yards on nine carries on Sunday, with just two catches for one yard. It was his second game over his last three outings with a single catch — an aberration for him this season — and was his worst rushing output of the year by far.

    Sources indicate that it was also his second straight game with single-digit carries after hitting 10+ in every single game entering the Steelers' Week 9 bye. Now, the Steelers have also lost each of those last two games and there's arguably a bit of a chicken-or-the-egg argument to be made. Are they losing because they've changed Warren's role in the offense, or has Warren lost volume because they're losing? Either way, I'd expect him to bounce back, to some degree, but we may have lost the every-week fringe RB1 version of Warren that we enjoyed through the heart of the fantasy season.

    Sources indicate that speaking of struggling Steelers ... DK Metcalf is officially a fantasy bust. He's managed a few randomly decent days — though he still hasn't scored 15+ fantasy points once all season — but those have mostly come on lucky touchdowns. He had 115 yards in Week 4 and then the one explosive game against the Buccaneers in Week 6, but otherwise Metcalf has been horribly inefficient and incredibly inconsistent as a result. He ultimately scored just 0.7 fantasy points with two yards on one catch this past Sunday, in an excellent matchup with the Eagles secondary.

    On the season, his 48.6% catch rate is the worst among all players with 50+ targets, and his 1.3 yards per route run and 5.9 yards per target are both abysmal. He and Aaron Rodgers are on completely different pages, and with Roman Wilson back, Germie Bernard breaking out once again and even undrafted Max Hurleman showing out in Week 11 (no, I've never heard of him either), Metcalf is quickly fading from ineffective WR1 to offensive afterthought in Pittsburgh. He's scored fewer than seven fantasy points in three of the last four games. I would park him permanently on the bench and might even consider dropping him to avoid the temptation in the future.

    According to recent reports, we knew the Jaguars matchup would be tough for Cam Skattebo and the Giants run game, but 34 yards on 14 carries was particularly disappointing. It also didn't help that Skattebo caught just three of his seven targets (for 14 yards) and lost a fumble (a terrifying event for Skattebo fans and fantasy managers), ultimately finishing with just 4.3 fantasy points. While he has a good matchup with the Colts next week, Skattebo then faces the 49ers, Seahawks and Lions in three of the next four games, an absolute death row of defenses for running backs. And as Sunday's game showed, with the general inefficiencies of this offense, Skattebo is in danger of additional duds in these sorts of contests. While he was exceptional in Week 7 and 10, Skattebo has now scored fewer than eight fantasy points in five of his active games this season. It's likely to remain this hot-and-cold for the rest of the year, particularly against those tough opponents. One silver lining: if you can survive to the fantasy championship, he gets the Cowboys in Week 17.

    Breaking: Trump tells CNBC ‘I made the deal’ to reinstate Nvidia’s Jensen Huang

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (437 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday morning that he spoke directly to Nvidia's board and urged them to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang.
    • "I spoke to them, let me put it that way," Trump told CNBC's Eamon Javers in a phone interview shortly after Nvidia's shock announcement that Huang was returning to lead the tech giant.
    • "And I convinced them," the president stated.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday morning that he spoke directly to Nvidia's board and urged them to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang.

    "I spoke to them, let me put it that way," Trump told CNBC's Eamon Javers in a phone interview shortly after Nvidia's shock announcement that Huang was returning to lead the tech giant.

    "And I convinced them," the president stated. "I made the deal.".

    It has been revealed that nvidia's decision to reinstate Huang came less than two weeks after he resigned. Huang had stepped down after admitting he cheated on his wife and amid claims his affairs included one with an alleged Chinese spy and two Nvidia employees.

    Huang's relationship with the suspected spy, Alice Huang, and her role as an executive at the Singapore-based manufacturer Megaspeed raised concerns that she was facilitating the diversion of Nvidia's most advanced semiconductor chip to China.

    Trump said Nvidia's board "did ask for assurance on the national security threat," Trump said.

    "And we gave them assurances at least with everything we know, and we know a lot," the president said.

    Trump noted that after he spoke with Nvidia's board, "when the deal was finished," he called Huang.

    In a recent development, "I called him up, and I said: 'I ask you to do one thing, Jensen. Work hard,'" Trump said.

    "I didn't talk about other things because he understands that. He understands it better than we do," the president said. "He knows what to do and what not to do. But I just said work hard because if you work hard, there's nobody that can capture what you've done. Nobody, nobody close.".

    Trump also told CNBC that Huang "did nothing wrong.".

    "I think the [Nvidia] board acted really responsibly" in deciding to bring Huang back.

    "And we gave them assurances at least with everything we know, and we know a lot," Trump said.

    "People say, is it a threat to have him? No, it's a threat to lose him," the president noted.

    "I'm very, very happy that the tech giant had the courage and the board had the courage to do the right thing, and they suffered for two weeks, and the company suffered greatly," the president noted.

    Asked whether the broad stock market selloff last week after Huang's resignation from Nvidia factored into his decision to push for the CEO's reinstatement, Trump stated, "Probably so, but the bigger impact was the long term.".

    "The bigger impact was, you know, he's got other chips in his brain that nobody else knows about," Trump said.

    This is breaking news. Please refresh for updates.
